gaps.title: A medicine the patient takes but this organization did not prescribe cannot be recorded
gaps.scenario: A new patient in the IM clinic brings atorvastatin from a cardiologist and metformin from another practice. The nurse must put them on the medication list for reconciliation and interaction checks. With no Pharmacy pack, write_prescription(action=start) prints and stores it as a prescription this clinician wrote (patient_medications.prescriber_id = the nurse's doctor). In a hospital with a live dispense service the same write sends a dispensing request to Pharmacy for a drug nobody here prescribed. Epic separates 'patient-reported' / outside medications from orders and reconciles them at every admission and discharge.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 04, prescription: 'A prescription is a **request** exactly when the organization has a live `dispense` service the caller's department is served by; then `requests` gets a row to that department … Without one it is a paper script'; write_prescription action is 'start | change | stop' only; patient_medications carries 'prescriber_id' and no provenance column; entries.source describes who typed the row, not who prescribed.
gaps.fix: Add action = record (a medicine reported, not prescribed): no requests row whatever services exist, prescriber_id NULL, display line 'Atorvastatin 40 mg OD (reported)'; add one column patient_medications.is_prescribed_here (or source: prescribed | reported). It is Phase-0 because the list table and the request rule are being built now, and every row written before the column exists has ambiguous provenance forever.
gaps.skeptic: The clinical need is real and day-one for the IM clinic (reconciliation of a new patient's outside drugs), and spec 04's `write_prescription(… action start | change | stop …)` gives no honest way to write it: with a live `dispense` service the row goes to Pharmacy ('A prescription is a request exactly when the organization has a live dispense service'). But the mechanism already exists and the specialist's fix is wrong in both halves. Spec 01 already has `entries.source = outside` and the convention 'Outside and import also carry data.stated_author_name' (01 appendix), and spec 04's `write_result` already uses exactly this mode ('Outside result … write_result with request_id NULL, source = outside, data.source_name'). The fix is the same mode on `write_prescription` (a parameter with a default: signatures only grow), one clause on the request rule ('… and source = staff'), and the updater setting `prescriber_id` NULL for an outside entry. No new action, no new column. 'Every row written before the column exists has ambiguous provenance forever' is false: `patient_medications` is a derived table ('Deletable and rebuildable; nobody writes them directly'), so a later `source` column is filled by `rebuild_record` from the entry. Nothing locked changes; it should land before the first clinic goes live, not before Phase 0.

gaps.title: Free text on a non-consult request is refused, so a lab or imaging request cannot carry clinical details
gaps.scenario: A doctor requests a chest X-ray '? left lower lobe pneumonia, 3 days productive cough' or a CBC 'on warfarin, post-transfusion'. Radiology justification (IR(ME)R in the UK/EU, ACR in the US) is legally required and every lab request form has a clinical-details box. Under 04 the set is refused at Done. The printed request to an outside imaging provider (spec 05 'Print … a result') carries no indication.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 04, request: 'Refuses: service retired or not offered to the caller's department (spec 02 `served`), `patient_merged`, `patient_died`, a `question_text` on a non-consult service.' This contradicts spec 04 rule 4: 'Refusals are structural only.'
gaps.fix: Drop the refusal: every request accepts `text` (spec 01's convention 'typed text only in keys text/*_text'), keep question_text as the consult-only key or fold both into text. A one-line change in write_request now; later it means rewriting the golden display-line fixtures and the request-surface banner that show it.
gaps.skeptic: The refusal is real and self-contradictory: spec 04 'Refuses: … a question_text on a non-consult service' against its own rule 4 'Refusals are structural only', and spec 01's convention 'typed text only in keys text/*_text' already licenses `data.text` on any entry. But nothing about it is Phase-0: `write_request`'s signature does not change (drop one clause in the body, or accept the existing `question_text` on every service), no table changes, and the request display line (`CBC`) never showed the text so no golden fixture is rewritten. For the IM clinic sending imaging out, `problems[]` (coded, with names) carries the indication today; the free-text box matters when an in-house Imaging pack or a printed outside request needs it. One-line amendment at leisure, not a build blocker.

gaps.title: The closed frequency set refuses regimens an IM clinic writes daily
gaps.scenario: Denosumab every 6 months, B12 every 3 months, alendronate weekly (ok), prednisolone alternate days, erythropoietin three times a week, warfarin '5 mg Mon/Wed/Fri, 2.5 mg other days', insulin titration. None of these is in the set; the whole Done set fails ('a failed Done writes nothing'). The clinician's only way through is to lie in the structured field ('monthly') and explain in instructions_text.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 04, prescription: 'Refuses: … a `frequency` outside the core set (`OD BD TDS QDS q4h q6h q8h q12h weekly monthly PRN once stat`)'; decide-now 'the core frequency set'. Again against rule 4, 'Refusals are structural only.'
gaps.fix: Make frequency free text validated only for non-empty, with the core set as the picker's suggestions and the trend/MAR logic treating an unknown value as 'other'; or add `other` requiring instructions_text. Phase-0 because if patient_medications.frequency is minted as an enum or CHECK now, relaxing it later is a column rewrite.
gaps.skeptic: The clinical point stands: B12 3-monthly, denosumab 6-monthly, alternate-day prednisolone and thrice-weekly EPO are weekly IM-clinic prescriptions, and the only way through the locked set (`OD BD TDS QDS q4h q6h q8h q12h weekly monthly PRN once stat`) is to lie in the structured field; `PRN` also appears both as a frequency value and as the separate `prn` boolean. But the 'column rewrite' argument is wrong. `patient_medications` is derived and rebuildable, so an enum → text change or a dropped CHECK on it costs a rebuild, not a rewrite; `data` is 'validated by the type's JSON schema (shipped in code, versioned by schema_version)' and spec 06 says 'a data-shape change bumps schema_version and the renderer reads both; old entries never migrate'. Adding `other` (requiring `instructions_text`) is an `ADD VALUE`. Fix it in the same spec-04 amendment as gap 1, before go-live; it does not gate Phase 0.

gaps.title: A pack has no outbound door: nothing can leave the database from a pack
gaps.scenario: Pharmacy must send an e-prescription to an external pharmacy or a national e-Rx hub; Billing must submit an insurance claim or check eligibility; Imaging must post to a modality worklist/PACS and fetch the report; a reminder SMS; notifiable-disease reporting; a bidirectional analyser that receives orders. Epic does all of this through Bridges/Interconnect. The pack contract lists a database side and a client side only; the pack role cannot reach net, and Edge Functions appear in core only for invite_user.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 02, Packs: 'no USAGE on another schema (`net`, `extensions`, `vault`, `storage`, `auth`, `cron`, `realtime`, another pack)'; spec 06: 'The role holds: EXECUTE on core.write_entry, core.change_request, core.record_settings_change, the gates, and every public read_… and mark_…; ALL on its own schema. Nothing else.' Spec 06 'What a pack ships' has no row for an Edge Function or an outbound job.
gaps.fix: Additive: one core funnel core.send_out(pack, kind, payload) that writes a core-owned outbox (same shape and runner discipline as pack_calls: tries, back-off, parked, shown on the Organization page) drained by one core Edge Function or pg_net job per organization; the pack sees the response as a later after_write-style call. Decide the shape now so the Pharmacy and Billing specs do not each invent one.
gaps.skeptic: Genuinely absent and genuinely unfillable by a pack: spec 02 and 06 deny `pack_<key>` USAGE on `net`, `vault`, `cron` and every foreign schema, B9 pins `service_role` to `create_organization` and `link_login` 'and no table privilege anywhere', and spec 06's 'What a pack ships' has no row for an Edge Function or a job — so an e-Rx hub, an insurer claim or a reminder SMS cannot be sent from anywhere a pack can reach. Not a Phase-0 item: nothing locked changes (a new core function, a new core-owned outbox table, one job), and the IM clinic on day one sends nothing out. Reject the 'decide the shape now' half: that is exactly the speculative structure the owner refuses. Add one line to 06's 'Written as rules now, built later' — 'outbound is a core door, never a pack's own' — and design it with the first pack spec (Pharmacy or Billing) that has a real endpoint.

gaps.title: core.write_entry's signature is unspecified, so whether a pack type can be a request (have a queue) is unknown
gaps.scenario: Imaging wants an imaging_request with laterality, contrast, pregnancy status and indication; Admissions wants a bed request; Blood bank wants a crossmatch request with product and units. Each needs a requests row (destination, priority, due_at, steps) born from a pack type. Laboratory avoids the question by using core's request and result, but Imaging cannot. Phase 0 builds the funnel and spec 06 test 10 freezes its signature ('Signatures only grow').
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 01, Functions: '`write_…` one public function per entry type → all end in the private write_entry' with no signature given; entry_types is 'key · name · pack · list · retired_at' with no request/reply marker; spec 04: 'What a type *does* is its behaviours (spec 01): request · reply · values · current · files' — spec 01 defines no such list, and 'behaviour' is on spec 01's 'Not used in the schema' list.
gaps.fix: Write the funnel in spec 01: core.write_entry(entry core.entries, request core.requests null, values core.entry_values[], files core.entry_files[]) and one sentence: 'any type may carry a destination; a non-NULL request makes it a request'. Then every pack knows it can ship a queued type without touching core.
gaps.skeptic: The question is already answered, so 'unknown' overstates it: 01 appendix section d says 'be a request | it has a requests row, because it had a destination' — request-ness is per entry, not per type — and core's own `prescription` ('request (when a dispensing service exists)') proves the funnel must accept a destination on a non-`request` type. Spec 04's 'behaviours (spec 01)' is a loose citation of that table, not a missing enum. What is genuinely missing is one sentence the migration author needs before writing the funnel: how `write_entry` learns the destination (a parameter `{to_department_id, priority, due_at}` or the `data` keys `write_request` already sets) and that a non-NULL destination on any type inserts the `requests` row via `change_request`'s `sent` step. Because `core.write_entry` is EXECUTE-granted to every pack role and 'Signatures only grow', getting it right at creation avoids a second overload forever. Zero delay: add the sentence to 01's Functions block, then start Phase 0.

gaps.title: The co-signature convention the appendix promises is not expressible with the locked note type
gaps.scenario: A resident writes a history and physical; the attending must co-sign, and medical records must find unsigned ones. The 01 appendix says a trainee note 'is itself a request', but under 04 a note has no request behaviour and a request cannot point at an entry. The workaround is a set [note, request to a 'Co-signature' consult service] with the attending replying note kind=consult_reply is_final; the only link between the note and its co-sign request is written_with_id, and read_to_review shows the request, not the note.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 01 appendix, conventions: 'A trainee note is itself a request to the `Co-signature` service.' vs spec 04 table: '`note` | reply (kind `consult_reply`) · values · files | consult request' and 'Any other kind refuses `reply_to_id`'; write_request(id, patient_id, visit_id, service_id, priority, due_at, question_text, problems[], to_department_id) has no pointer to the entry under review.
gaps.fix: Additive under spec 01 rule 1 ('A new fact is a key in data'): data.about_entry_id on a request, honoured by read_to_review and the request surface (show the note being reviewed). No column, no signature change; write the convention into 04 so the Co-signature service is a preset row, not folklore.
gaps.skeptic: Two of the appendix's three co-signature conventions work today: 'A trainee consult reply is a preliminary reply, and the attending writes the final' is `write_note(kind consult_reply, is_final false)` then the attending's final; 'Supervised orders carry responsible_id' is a column. Only 'A trainee note is itself a request to the Co-signature service' fails through `write_note`'s signature (no `service_id`). The workaround the specialist describes — a set [note, request to a `Co-signature` service], joined by `written_with_id`, with the attending's reply closing it and `read_to_review` finding unsigned ones — breaks no rule and is how the appendix meant it. The clean later fix follows appendix d, not a new key: `write_note` gains `service_id` (signature grows) and a note with a destination is a request. Do not invent `data.about_entry_id`. Training hospitals only; awkward, not blocking.

gaps.title: No pack slot on the core banner or record column, so pack-kept facts are invisible where prescribing happens
gaps.scenario: Obstetrics keeps pregnancies; an IM doctor on the core clinic screen starts an ACE inhibitor for a woman who is 14 weeks pregnant and never sees it — the banner shows allergies only. Admissions keeps code status (DNACPR); the clinic doctor never sees it. Epic's Storyboard shows pregnancy, code status, isolation, care team and FYI flags to every user. Packs may register department screens only for department types they ship and renderers only for their own types; the clinic screen is core's.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 05, visit: 'banner: name · age/sex · record number · ⚠ allergies (always) · died · open requests'; spec 06 client side: 'exports `{ key, departmentScreens, renderers, servicesColumns, presetFragment, actions }`'; spec 06 known limit: 'a pack cannot add a column to a core settings page beyond the one `servicesColumns` slot'. read_record's 'visit: the caller's department's open visit for this patient, or null' likewise hides an open admission from the clinic.
gaps.fix: Client-only, additive, same idea as servicesColumns: bannerItems and recordPanels slots in src/packs/<key>/index.ts, each fed by the pack's own <key>_read_… call; core draws them in a fixed place. Also let read_record.open_visits list every open visit the caller may read:queue (a nullable addition to the shape).
gaps.skeptic: 'Never sees it' is overstated. Spec 05 rule 4 'Every screen renders every type' and `read_record.entries` (the last 30 timeline cards) put an Obstetrics `pregnancy` entry on the IM doctor's visit screen, and the Obstetrics screen writes its set as the user so it can add a core `problem` ('Pregnant, EDD …') that sits in the RECORD column beside the drug list; code status is likewise a problem or a note. Spec 06 already names the restriction as a known limit ('a pack cannot add a column to a core settings page beyond the one servicesColumns slot'), so this is an accepted limit, not an omission. The fix is client-only and additive (`bannerItems` / `recordPanels` in `src/packs/<key>/index.ts`, same idea as `servicesColumns`), touching no table or function; do it when the first pack keeping a safety-relevant list (Obstetrics) is specced. `read_patients` already returns `open_visits[]` for any department the caller may `read:queue`, so an open admission is not hidden from the desk.

gaps.title: A booked clinic cannot see its queue in appointment order, and a Bookings pack cannot touch the core clinic queue
gaps.scenario: A clinic runs 08:00–12:00 in ten-minute slots. A 09:40 patient arrives at 08:30 and sits at the top of WAITING above the 08:40 patient who arrives at 08:35. The planned Bookings pack keeps its own bookings table, but the clinic department type is core's, its queue screen is core's, and 'Order in a band is arrival' is locked. Epic's Cadence schedule drives the Hyperspace department appointment desk order.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 05, queue: '**Patients** in bands — back · waiting · pending · in consult — urgent first, then arrival'; spec 03: 'Order in a band is arrival.' and decide-now 'no `scheduled_at` ever'; spec 03 later: 'a bookings pack whose `bookings` point at the visit they became'.
gaps.fix: Client-only: a queueColumns/queueSort slot in the pack index (fed by bookings_read_today(department_id)) that the core queue screen applies within a band; no column on visits, no rule change. State it in 05 so the Bookings pack is not designed around a duplicate department type.
gaps.skeptic: The locked rules govern the server query ('Order in a band is arrival', 'no scheduled_at ever') and should stay: the queue is who is present, and any clinician can click any patient in any order. What is missing is only a presentation hook: `read_visit_queue` rows carry no booking time, and a Bookings pack ships 'screens per department type' it owns, so it cannot re-sort core's `clinic` queue. A client-only `queueColumns` / stable in-band re-sort slot fed by `bookings_read_today` is additive, changes no column or rule, and belongs with the Bookings pack spec, stated in 05 then. Not a Phase-0 concern and not a hospital blocker: arrival order is how most walk-in-plus-booked clinics already call patients.

gaps.title: Vitals are eight fixed fields: no glucose, pain score, GCS, urine output or head circumference
gaps.scenario: The IM clinic nurse takes a capillary glucose and a pain score at every diabetic visit; a ward needs AVPU/GCS and urine output for NEWS2; paediatrics needs head circumference and MUAC. Today the nurse must either write a note with a coded form field or write a request-plus-result pair for one fingerprick. Epic flowsheets are row-configurable.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 04, vitals: 'write_vitals(id, patient_id, visit_id, occurred_at, systolic, diastolic, pulse, respiratory_rate, temperature, spo2, weight, height)' and rule 1 'One function, one type, one shape.'
gaps.fix: Additive overload (allowed by spec 06 test 10): write_vitals(…, values[] of {code, value_number, unit}) where each code must exist in codes, exactly as note form fields already do; latest_vitals and read_values need no change because entry_values already trends any code.
gaps.skeptic: Two rule-abiding paths exist today, both stated: a nurse note whose form has a coded numeric field ('numeric fields with a code become values[] and trend', spec 04 note), and a point-of-care service with `service_fields` written as request + result (which also gets ranges and flags, the right shape for a fingerprick glucose). NEWS2/GCS is the Admissions pack; head circumference and MUAC are Paediatrics — spec 04 already says 'a paediatrics or emergency pack may write flags'. The additive overload `write_vitals(…, values[] of {code, value_number, unit})` is allowed by 'Signatures only grow' and needs no change to `latest_vitals` or `read_values`; add it when the IM pack's forms show the note-form path is too clumsy for a nurse. Not Phase-0.

gaps.title: Unsigned work is invisible to everyone but its author
gaps.scenario: A doctor sees twelve patients, presses Back to queue on three, and goes home. Their notes exist only as drafts rows; the visits sit in waiting/in_consult until the 12-hour sweep marks them pending; the record shows nothing for those consults; the next day's clinician, the department head and medical records have no way to see who owes what. Epic's In Basket Chart Completion and deficiency tracking exist for exactly this.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 05 rule 3: 'Today is a draft until Done. Everything typed in a consult is a `drafts` row'; known limit: 'drafts are per user (two users editing one visit each see their own Today)'; spec 01: 'drafts entry_id · author_id · patient_id · visit_id · type · service_id · reply_to_id · data' with no read function for anyone but the author in 01–05.
gaps.fix: Additive: read_drafts(organization_id, department_id) returning {author, patient, visit, count, oldest updated_at} for read:queue holders, and an 'unsigned' count in the queue footer beside 'done today'. No column change.
gaps.skeptic: Half of this is by design and stays: drafts are private ('drafts are per user', spec 05 known limit) and 'Nothing half-written is ever in the record'. The real, small hole is operational, not clinical: after the sweep ('seen ∧ open ∧ … idle 12 h → pending, away') the three visits leave `read_visit_queue` (`present_at IS NOT NULL`) and survive only as the footer count 'away (open, not present)' with no read that lists them by assignee. Fix is one additive read or a parameter on `read_visit_queue` (include away) so the head sees 'Dr X · 3 open visits'; no column, no rule. `read_drafts` is the wrong shape — nobody but the author should see the draft text. Epic's deficiency tracking is Epic-has-it; the IM clinic's next-day check is 'who has open visits'.

gaps.title: Shapes Phase 0 must create are undefined or contradicted across the locked specs
gaps.scenario: The migration author has to create flowsheets with no columns given; templates.items must hold both request sets and note forms with coded fields ('tier 2' in 04, but 'tier' is on 01's not-used list) with no shape; service_fields.kind has no value list; request data copies 'service {id, code, name, kind, department_name}' but services has no kind; 05 says the department switcher is 'staff_active_department (spec 02)' while 02's appendix lists that name as rejected; 03 says 'Today's fields are vitals, note and triage entries' while 04 says 'Nine types, no more in core' with no triage; core.record_numbers and erasures appear only in appendices.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 01 tables: '`flowsheets`' in the Settings row, defined nowhere ('as in v3'); spec 04 note: '`fields` is the filled form of a structured template (spec 02 tier 2)'; spec 05: 'the choice is `staff_active_department` (spec 02)' vs spec 02 appendix: 'Names rejected at final: … `staff_active_department`'; spec 03: 'acuity is a triage entry and `priority` its three-level shadow'.
gaps.fix: One short amendment: define flowsheets (or drop it until a pack needs it), give templates.items its two item shapes, list service_fields.kind values, remove services.kind from request data, make the department choice a client localStorage key in 05, and change 03's 'triage entries' to 'a triage type a pack ships'. Nothing clinical, but every one of these is a table or a fixture Phase 0 writes.
gaps.skeptic: Only one of the seven items stops a migration: `flowsheets` appears in 01's and 02's Settings rows and in `read_organization`'s return with no columns anywhere ('as in v3'; v3 is not in the repo), and no function in 01–06 reads it. The migration author would have to invent columns — speculative structure — so the one-line fix is to strike it from both lists until a pack (the IM pack's trend sets) needs it; nothing else references it. The rest are doc slips with no migration impact, fixable in any amendment pass: `templates.items` is already `jsonb` (02 appendix) and its two item shapes are a client/JSON-schema matter for the Templates screen; `service_fields.kind` values are implied by `kind, unit, choices` (number | text | choice) and an enum grows by `ADD VALUE`; `services.kind` in spec 04's request `data` is a slip for `reply_type`; `staff_active_department` in 05 is a client localStorage key that 02 rightly rejected as a column; 03's 'triage entries' means the emergency pack's type per its own appendix (Y6). `core.record_numbers` and `erasures` are defined with columns in the 03 and 01 appendices and named in 03's table list and 01's upkeep line, so they are not undefined.

gaps.title: The public write functions omit the entry header write_entry has
gaps.scenario: A patient brings a lab report from another hospital: `write_result` with `request_id NULL` has no `patient_id`, no `visit_id`, no `source`, no `source_name`, no `occurred_at`, so the function as written cannot say whose result it is. A ward nurse writing a late entry at 06:00 for events at 02:00: `write_note` has no `occurred_at`. An analyser re-send: `write_result` has no `source_key`. A resident's note the attending is responsible for: nothing sets `responsible_id`. A lab issuing a corrected result, or a clinician amending a note: no `write_<type>` takes `replaces_id`, so the documented same-type correction path is unreachable and every correction must be a strike plus a new entry. A legacy import of ten years of notes would all carry `occurred_at = now()`.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04: `write_result(id, request_id, values[], text, is_final, not_done, not_done_reason_text, files[])` beside "**Outside result** (a PDF from elsewhere): `write_result` with `request_id NULL`, `source = outside`, `data.source_name`, `files[]`"; `write_note(id, patient_id, visit_id, kind, text, fields, problems[], reply_to_id, is_final, files[])` with no `occurred_at`; only `write_vitals` takes `occurred_at`; only `write_entered_in_error` takes `replaces_id`. Spec 01 `entries`: "occurred_at (clinical time) · recorded_at (system time)", "source (staff | patient | machine | outside | import) · source_key", "closed columns incl. `responsible_id`". 01 appendix: "replace another entry | `replaces_id` (a correction, an update of a preliminary entry, or type `entered_in_error`)" and "A retired type, or a type whose pack is off, accepts only entries carrying `replaces_id`".
gaps.fix: Give every `write_<type>` one shared tail, all nullable: `occurred_at, source, source_key, source_name, responsible_id, replaces_id`; give `write_result` `patient_id` and `visit_id` (required when `request_id` is NULL). `write_set` items pass them through unchanged. These are the function signatures Phase 0 freezes under "public signatures only grow", so it is cheaper now than as nine overloads later.
gaps.skeptic: Two of the five claims are outright contradictions inside locked text, and both are Phase 0 deliverables. (1) Spec 04 `write_result(id, request_id, values[], text, is_final, not_done, not_done_reason_text, files[])` beside "**Outside result**: `write_result` with `request_id NULL`, `source = outside`, `data.source_name`" — with `request_id` NULL nothing names the patient, so the outside-result path that spec 01 rule 5 calls a core review loop is unreachable as written. (2) Same-type correction is a core mechanism the specs depend on: 01 appendix `display_line` "'Corrected: …' when it replaces a final entry", the lookup order "3. By `replaces_id`. It raises `already_replaced`", "A retired type, or a type whose pack is off, accepts only entries carrying `replaces_id`", spec 06 test 7 "accepts a correction with the pack disabled" and checklist fixture "one replaced, one struck" — yet the only public function in spec 04 taking `replaces_id` is `write_entered_in_error`. Strike-plus-new cannot satisfy the retired-type rule (the new entry is refused), so a lab's corrected CBC on day one is expressible only by breaking a locked rule. The other three (`occurred_at`, `source_key`, `responsible_id`) are columns spec 01 already defines with their semantics ("write_entry sets it to recorded_at − age; absolute only when picked by hand"; T17 analyser re-send; "Supervised orders carry `responsible_id`"), so this is not new structure: it is one sentence in spec 04 — every `write_<type>` takes the entry header after `id, patient_id, visit_id` (age or `occurred_at`, `source_key`, `responsible_id`, `replaces_id`, all nullable; `source` follows `users.kind` for machine and importer, hand-set only as `outside` on `write_result`, which also needs `patient_id`/`visit_id` when `request_id` is NULL). It belongs before Phase 0 only because spec 06 test 10 "Signatures only grow" would otherwise leave nine dead overloads in the golden file forever; the build delay is zero.

gaps.title: Clinical details are refused on every non-consult request
gaps.scenario: The IM clinic orders a chest X-ray: radiology requires clinical information and the question ("? pneumonia, 3 weeks cough, smoker"), by law in many jurisdictions (IR(ME)R justification). A wound swab needs the site and the antibiotic the patient is on. A histology request needs the clinical summary. `write_request` refuses `question_text` for all of these because the service is not a consult, and an imaging or laboratory pack cannot add a key to the core `request` type's `data`.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 `request`: "Refuses: service retired or not offered to the caller's department (spec 02 `served`), `patient_merged`, `patient_died`, a `question_text` on a non-consult service." Spec 04 rule 4: "Refusals are structural only." This refusal is not structural.
gaps.fix: Delete the refusal. Keep the parameter, or rename it `text` per the spec 01 convention ("typed text only in keys `text`/`*_text`"), and let the request surface show it under the question on every service. No table changes.
gaps.skeptic: Spec 04 `request`: "Refuses: … a `question_text` on a non-consult service" contradicts spec 04's own rule 4 "Refusals are structural only" and spec 05's request surface, which draws "the request's question" for every request, not only consults. The first-target IM clinic sends a chest X-ray outside (`services.department_id NULL`) on day one and the printed request must carry the clinical question; today it can only be smuggled into `problems[]` codes or a sibling `note` in the same `write_set`, which the receiving department's surface does not show. No table, column or signature changes: strike the sentence before `write_request` is written. I keep it before Phase 0 only because it is a rule Phase 0 would otherwise build and test; removing it later is safe but pointless work. The parameter name (`question_text` or `text`) is the owner's call and does not matter.

gaps.title: The prescription frequency set refuses real regimens
gaps.scenario: ICU: noradrenaline 0.1 mcg/kg/min continuous, titrated to MAP. Oncology: cisplatin day 1 and day 8 of a 21-day cycle. Dialysis: erythropoietin three times weekly with dialysis. Psychiatry: a depot antipsychotic every four weeks, denosumab six-monthly. Ward: warfarin alternate days, antibiotics q1h or q2h post-transplant. Each is refused by `write_prescription`. The only escape is a pack type (`icu_infusion`), which does not feed `patient_medications`, so the banner's medication list on the ward would omit the vasopressor.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 `prescription`: "Refuses: ... a `frequency` outside the core set (`OD BD TDS QDS q4h q6h q8h q12h weekly monthly PRN once stat`)". Decide-now item: "the core frequency set". Spec 04 rule 3 already validates drug and problem codes "by form only"; frequency is the one clinical code validated by a closed list.
gaps.fix: Make `frequency` a `frequency:<code>` string validated by form, with the core set shipped as global `codes` rows of kind `frequency` (spec 02 rule 1, "Settings are rows"), and add `continuous` and `frequency_text` (required when the code is `other`) so a cycle schedule is expressible in words. The updater copies the code into `patient_medications.frequency` unchanged; nothing else moves. Decide the shape now because `patient_medications.frequency` and the JSON schema are Phase 0.
gaps.skeptic: The clinical point stands for the first target, not only ICU: an IM clinic prescribes B12 every three months, denosumab six-monthly, alternate-day warfarin, five-days-a-week doses, none in `OD BD TDS QDS q4h q6h q8h q12h weekly monthly PRN once stat`, and choosing `OD` with the truth in `instructions_text` makes `display_line` ("Metformin 1 g BD") lie. But the fix is not a Phase 0 shape. Widening a JSON-schema enum and adding an optional `frequency_text` (required when the code is `other`) is a superset: old entries stay valid, no renderer needs two shapes, `patient_medications.frequency` is a text column, and spec 06 Upgrade already prices it ("a data-shape change bumps `schema_version`"). Spec 04 built-later "structured dose sigs for e-prescribing" and spec 01 built-later "inpatient dose charts (rule 6)" cover the infusion and cycle cases when a ward or oncology exists. The `frequency:<code>` codes-table design the specialist proposes is speculative structure. Phase 0's only obligation: `frequency` is `text`, not a Postgres enum. Land the wider set before the first clinic goes live, as prescription schema_version 2 if it slips past Phase 0.

gaps.title: write_vitals is eight fixed fields; a ward obs chart needs more
gaps.scenario: Ward observations every four hours must produce NEWS2, which needs consciousness (ACVPU) and whether the patient is on supplemental oxygen; neither is a parameter. Paediatrics needs head circumference and length; ED needs pain score, capillary glucose and GCS; the ward needs urine output. A ward or paediatrics pack must therefore ship its own observations type that duplicates `vitals`, and `read_record.latest_vitals` ("the newest vitals entry's values") then shows the clinic's reading from last month rather than the 10-minute-old ward obs.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04: `write_vitals(id, patient_id, visit_id, occurred_at, systolic, diastolic, pulse, respiratory_rate, temperature, spo2, weight, height)`; "Codes are fixed LOINC"; "a paediatrics or emergency pack may write flags" (but not new fields). Spec 04 `read_record`: "latest_vitals  the newest vitals entry's values".
gaps.fix: `write_vitals(id, patient_id, visit_id, occurred_at, values[])` where each value's code must be in a core-shipped LOINC list (the current eight plus consciousness, supplemental oxygen, pain, capillary glucose, head circumference, urine output). BMI still computed; still no flags in core; `latest_vitals` unchanged. Same one-function-one-type rule, just not positional.
gaps.skeptic: Everything named is expressible today without touching core. Spec 04 `note`: "numeric fields with a code become `values[]` and trend" — pain score, capillary glucose, GCS, urine output are coded fields on a nurse-note template and trend through `read_values(patient_id, codes[])` beside the vitals codes, because values are keyed by `codes.code`, not by entry type. A ward or paediatrics pack ships an observations type with the LOINC codes it needs (spec 04: "Packs needing structured clinical content with its own screen add a **type**"), and its NEWS2 screen reads `read_values`; two entry types carrying `loinc:8480-6` trend as one line by design. The one real loss, `read_record.latest_vitals` "the newest vitals entry's values" showing last month's clinic reading on a ward, is a read-side tweak (newest entry carrying the vitals codes) with no signature change, and it is a hospital-ward concern. "vitals codes fixed to LOINC" is a decide-now item the owner took; a positional-to-`values[]` signature change now would be an overload later and buys nothing for the IM clinic.

gaps.title: `flowsheets` is named in two specs and defined in none
gaps.scenario: ICU and ward want a 24-hour grid of codes over time. Spec 01 lists `flowsheets` among the settings tables and the 02 appendix says `read_organization` returns "templates, flowsheets", but no spec gives the table a column, a function or a screen. Phase 0 migrates the tables of 01-04 and cannot migrate this one.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01 Tables: "Settings | `entry_types` · `organization_packs` · `departments` · `services` · `service_fields` · `codes` · `flowsheets` · `templates` ...". 01 appendix: "`flowsheets` and `templates` are as in v3", and v3 is not among the six specs.
gaps.fix: Either one line in spec 01 (`flowsheets  id · organization_id · department_id null · name · codes[] · retired_at`, a named list of codes that `read_values` fills, saved by `save_flowsheet` under `manage:templates`) or strike the word from both tables and let the ICU pack keep its grids. Either is fine; an undefined table in a locked spec is not.
gaps.skeptic: Spec 01 Tables: "Settings | … `codes` · `flowsheets` · `templates` …"; spec 02 Tables: "`service_fields` · `codes` · `entry_types` · `flowsheets`   as in spec 01"; 01 appendix: "`flowsheets` and `templates` are as in v3" (v3 is not among the specs); 02 appendix `read_organization` returns "templates, flowsheets". No column, function, action or screen in 01–06 touches it, and Phase 0 migrates the tables of 01–04, so it must know whether this table exists. The owner rejects speculative structure, so the answer is the shorter one: strike the word from the two table lists and from `read_organization`. A 24-hour grid is a screen over `read_values(patient_id, codes[])`; the codes it shows are a `templates` row or the ICU pack's own setting, never a core table. Zero build cost, but it is a Phase 0 decision.

gaps.title: No patient-level alert reaches the banner
gaps.scenario: Palliative care records a DNACPR decision; the patient arrests on a ward or arrives in the ED. Infection control flags MRSA; safeguarding flags a child; cardiology notes a pacemaker before an MRI; the patient is anticoagulated; the patient is pregnant. Every one of these must be as visible as ⚠ allergies on every screen of every department, and none can be: the banner is core, `read_record` has no key for it, and a pack can neither add a type to core nor add anything to the banner.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05 visit screen: "banner: name · age/sex · record number · ⚠ allergies (always) · died · open requests". Spec 04 `read_record`: "patient  banner: names, record_number, sex, born_on, age, died_on, merged_into_id". Spec 04 decide-now: "Nine types, no more in core". Spec 06 known limits: "a pack cannot add a column to a core settings page beyond the one `servicesColumns` slot" and there is no banner slot at all.
gaps.fix: A tenth type `alert` on the exact pattern of `allergy`: `write_alert(id, patient_id, visit_id, action add|update|remove, alert_id, kind, text, files[])`, list `patient_alerts (id · organization_id · patient_id · kind · text · status · latest_entry_id)`, `read_record.alerts`, drawn beside allergies. Additive: a row in `entry_types`, one function, one derived table, one key in `read_record`. Decide the banner placement before the 05 screens are built so no pack invents its own.
gaps.skeptic: Every example is expressible today as a `problem`: `write_problem` takes `code` ("`icd10:E11` or NULL (uncoded allowed)"), so DNACPR (Z66), MRSA carrier (Z22.32), pacemaker (Z95.0), pregnant state (Z33.1), anticoagulated (visible in `medications` anyway) land in `patient_problems`, come back in `read_record.problems` for every department, sit in the RECORD region of every visit screen (spec 05: "problems (✓ ✎ ✕ + add)"), and are prefetched for the queue ("Opening a queue calls `read_record` for everyone present"). What is missing is only banner placement, and that is a client convention: spec 05's banner already raises "⚠ allergies (always)"; raising active problems whose code is in a small alert list is the same trick, no schema. A tenth type breaks the decide-now item "Nine types, no more in core" and is speculative; if three departments end up wanting a non-problem alert (safeguarding is the honest case, since it is not a diagnosis), it is additive then — a row in `entry_types`, one function, one list, one `read_record` key. Not before Phase 0, not "blocks-a-hospital".

gaps.title: No entry can be confidential to a department
gaps.scenario: Psychiatry's psychotherapy notes, a sexual-health visit, an adolescent's contraception consultation, an HIV result in a jurisdiction that ring-fences it: the therapist writes the note into the same record the orthopaedic registrar reads, and nothing in core lets a department keep an entry to itself. A pack cannot fix it because the rule is the read functions'.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01: "Every department reads and writes the same record ... nothing clinical lives outside the record." Spec 02 access: `read_record` passes on `read:record` "in that department or everywhere", with no per-entry filter. Spec 02 built later lists only "restricted records and `record_reads.reason_text`", which is the whole patient, not an entry.
gaps.fix: No new column (rule 1): `data.is_restricted = true` set through the shared header of the previous fix; `read_record`, `read_entries`, `read_entry`, `read_values` return such an entry only to a caller holding a new action `read:restricted` in `entries.department_id` (or everywhere), and to everyone else return the card as `{type, department_name, display_line: 'Restricted entry'}`. Lists (`patient_medications`, `patient_allergies`, `patient_problems`) are never restricted: clozapine must be visible in the ED. Additive on the read side; do it before the psychiatry pack.
gaps.skeptic: Correct that nothing in core hides an entry from a department and that no pack can, because the filter would sit in `read_record`, `read_entries`, `read_entry`, `read_values` (spec 01: "Every department reads and writes the same record"). But spec 02 built-later already plans the case the owner's named departments (internal medicine, cardiology, obstetrics, admissions) will meet first: "restricted records and `record_reads.reason_text`" — whole-patient restriction with break-the-glass. Per-entry restriction is a psychiatry or sexual-health need, speculative for two years, and nothing in Phase 0 forecloses it: it is a `data` key (rule 1), one new `actions` row (`read:restricted`), and a WHERE in four reads, with the lists (`patient_medications`, `patient_allergies`, `patient_problems`) deliberately never filtered so clozapine shows in the ED. Additive on the read side, and it lands with the first department that asks for it, not now. Severity is "awkward until psychiatry", not "blocks-a-hospital".

gaps.title: Registers and recalls: no backfill, no patient enumeration, no deferred requests
gaps.scenario: Primary care wants every diabetic with HbA1c over 9 and no visit in six months, every woman due a smear, every child due a vaccine, and a recall for each. A register pack can only be fed by `after_write` (an updater runs only on the pack's own types), and `after_write` is "never on rebuild", so a pack switched on a year after go-live sees no history; no read function enumerates patients (`read_patients` returns 20 rows for a query), so it cannot catch up on its own. A recall written today as a `request` due in ninety days sits in the clinic's request queue for ninety days (open by `due_at`) and blocks `retire_department`.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01 Packs table: after-write "Runs ... after the write has committed ... **never on rebuild**"; updater "Named by `entry_types.list`" (the entry's own type). Spec 06 lifecycle Enable: "`rebuild_record` replays existing entries through its updater" only. Spec 01 queue index: "`(to_department_id, priority, due_at) WHERE status = 'open'`". Spec 02: "`retire_department` is refused while the department has open requests". Spec 01 built later: "cross-patient search (a derived table)".
gaps.fix: One additive function `replay_pack_calls(organization_id, pack, since)` (`manage:organization`) that inserts a `pack_calls` row for every live entry since a date; the contract already makes `after_write` idempotent, so this is safe. Plus one queue rule: `read_queue` returns requests with `due_at` beyond a horizon (7 days) as a `later` count, and `retire_department` ignores them once re-routed. The cross-patient derived table already planned covers the rest.
gaps.skeptic: Two of three claims are already handled. The 90-day recall does not clog the queue: 01 appendix `read_queue(department_id, is_upcoming)` "By default it returns requests due by the end of today, plus `infinity` items", so a request due in 90 days is invisible until then, and `retire_department` refusing while it has open requests is correct (re-route them with `mark_routing`; a retired department must not swallow work). Registers over core `result` values are spec 01 built-later "cross-patient search (a derived table)" — a core public read over `entry_values (patient_id, code, value_number, occurred_at)`, which the IM pack's recall screen will need anyway; that is the stated plan and it needs no pack enumeration. What remains is real but small and additive: a pack enabled long after go-live whose data is fed by `after_write` ("**never on rebuild**") sees no history, and no read enumerates patients. A `replay_pack_calls(organization_id, pack, since)` under `manage:organization` is one function, safe because `after_write` is already idempotent on `entry_id`. It is not the first organization's problem (the IM pack ships with go-live), so core-later, and not a Phase 0 shape.

gaps.title: Corrections have no public door: replaces_id is on no write function
gaps.scenario: The lab amends Hb 9.2 to 12.9 after a clotted sample; a final culture report replaces the preliminary; a clinician fixes a wrong dose in a prescription entry or a typo in a signed note. Every one of these is 'a newer entry replaces it', and the only public function that takes replaces_id is write_entered_in_error. The clinic's only path is strike + retype, which breaks the C1 'Corrected:' thread, loses the request link on the new result, and makes every amended lab result look like a wrong-patient event.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04, all nine signatures, e.g. 'write_result(id, request_id, values[], text, is_final, not_done, not_done_reason_text, files[])' and 'write_note(id, patient_id, visit_id, kind, text, fields, problems[], reply_to_id, is_final, files[])' — no replaces_id — against spec 01 'the only thing that can ever happen to an entry is that a newer entry replaces it' and 01 appendix fixture 23 'a final replacing a preliminary' and C1 'corrected result after review… A correction sets review_needed_at'.
gaps.fix: Add 'replaces_id uuid default null' as the last parameter of every write_<type> (and pass it through write_set items). write_entry already handles it (UNIQUE (replaces_id), 'already_replaced'). Rule: type must equal the replaced entry's type (entered_in_error excepted); a replacement result inherits request_id; the display line gets the 'Corrected:' prefix. Must land before the golden signatures file is frozen, since 06 test 10 forbids losing a line and Phase 0 writes these bodies.
gaps.skeptic: Confirmed against the text. Spec 04 lists all nine signatures and only write_entered_in_error(id, replaces_id, reason_text) carries replaces_id; spec 04 rule 1 says 'One function, one type, one shape' and the 01 appendix says 'A public write_<type key> function exists per type. It only validates and shapes data' — there is no other door into write_entry. Yet same-type replacement is a designed core behaviour, not an option: 01 rule 3 ('one pattern for newer replaces older'), 01 appendix invariant 3 ('It keeps the same type, unless its type is entered_in_error. is_final may differ: a final report replaces a preliminary one'), invariant 13 (replacement cleanup, 'review_needed_at is set'), the display_line rule (''Corrected: …' when it replaces a final entry'), fixture 23 ('a prescription corrected after it was stopped … a final replacing a preliminary'), 01 line 124 and 06 test 7 ('accepts a correction with the pack disabled') and 06 lifecycle ('Retire a type … it accepts only replacements from then on'). One correction to the specialist: strike + retype does NOT lose the request link (write_result takes request_id and 'A closed request never refuses a reply'); what it loses is the version chain, the Corrected: prefix and the truth (a preliminary culture is not 'entered in error'), and if the lab does not strike, reply_flag = 'worst flag' over live replies keeps the wrong HH forever. Why before Phase 0 rather than later: Phase 0 writes fixture 23 and 06 test 7, which cannot be written without the parameter; and adding a defaulted parameter later means dropping the old overload (a 9-arg call would otherwise match both and Postgres raises 'function is not unique'), i.e. nine removed lines in the B17 golden file. Do it once, and in the same pass settle the rest of the generic tail 04 omits but 01 promises 'from day one': responsible_id (01 decide-now 'closed columns incl. responsible_id'; C4 verbal orders; 'Supervised orders carry responsible_id') appears on no 04 signature, nor does the act's age ('the client sends the age of an act, never its clock') except on write_vitals. Nine spec lines, zero build delay.

gaps.title: A request sent outside can never be answered, so send-outs never close
gaps.scenario: HbA1c sent to a reference lab; a referral letter to an external cardiologist whose reply letter comes back; a send-out histology. The result arrives as a PDF. The in-house lab tech or the requesting doctor tries to file it as the reply to the open send-out request. No staff member holds any role on the outside department, so write_result is refused. The only way to end the request is mark_step('cancelled') with a false reason, or file the result unlinked (request_id NULL) and leave read_sent_outside growing forever. Closing the loop on referrals, the one workflow spec 03 built read_sent_outside for, is not expressible.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 result: 'Caller must hold write:result in the request's to_department_id.' Spec 02: 'outside (created on first use; nobody holds a role there)'. Spec 06: 'Never a closing step: only a reply or a cancel ends a request.' 02 appendix O14 widened read:queue for outside destinations only: 'read:queue on an outside department for anyone holding it in the organization'; no such widening exists for write:<reply_type>. The appendix's 'Unsolicited outside results are filed as a set: the result, plus a Review result request' covers unsolicited results only.
gaps.fix: One more narrow widening in require_access, symmetric with O14: write:<the service's reply_type> on an is_outside department passes for anyone holding it anywhere in the organization. The reply carries source = outside and data.stated_author_name (already a convention). read_sent_outside rows gain an Answer button in the client. No table changes; but the gate's widening list and the tenant-matrix fixtures are written in Phase 0, so decide it now.
gaps.skeptic: The hole is real but narrower and the fix is additive. Spec 04 result: 'Caller must hold write:result in the request's to_department_id'; spec 02: outside is a department where 'nobody holds a role there'; the 02 appendix gate lists exactly 'Two widenings, both narrow', both for read:queue. So a per-department doctor or technician cannot reply to a send-out. The gap understates it: the step path is gated on to_department_id as well ('require_access(…, 'mark:' || step, patient_id, to_department_id)'), so the 'false cancel' escape is equally closed to them. But the gate also passes for a role held 'in department_id or everywhere', and user_roles.department_id NULL = everywhere, so the owner-doctor of the first-target clinic can file the reply today; the workflow is not inexpressible, it is confined to everywhere-holders. The fix is one OR clause in require_access mirroring O14 ('read:queue on an outside department for anyone holding it in the organization'), extended to write:<the service's reply_type> and mark:cancelled/mark:done on an is_outside destination, with source = outside and data.stated_author_name (01 appendix, an existing convention). No table, no signature; require_access is CREATE OR REPLACE'd in place and B16 'enumerates pg_proc at run time', so nothing frozen in Phase 0 has to be reopened. Corrected belongs: core-later, ideally the first release after Phase 0 since read_sent_outside exists precisely for this list.

gaps.title: Spec 04 says only critical results reach the requester; spec 01's rule says every final reply does
gaps.scenario: Creatinine 180 (flag H, not HH) on a patient not due back for three months; a normal CBC that the doctor should still close the loop on; a decline. Under the spec 04 sentence, review_needed_at is set only by HH/LL, so an abnormal-but-not-critical result never appears in anyone's to-review list; the only way it is seen is the patient coming back. Missed abnormal results are the single most common outpatient safety failure.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 result: 'entries.flag is the worst of them; HH/LL sets review_needed_at (spec 01).' versus 01 appendix: 'a reply that needs review, which by default means is_final OR flag > 'normal'' and spec 05 footer: 'my results (read_to_review, count in red when a critical is waiting)', which presupposes non-critical rows in the list.
gaps.fix: Amend the spec 04 sentence to the 01 appendix rule: every final reply, every flagged reply, every correction and every decline sets review_needed_at; HH/LL is what turns the count red. Add one golden fixture: a normal final CBC appears in the requester's read_to_review. This is a rule inside change_request's fold and is built in Phase 0.
gaps.skeptic: It is a wording contradiction, not a structural gap, and 01 already wins. Spec 04: 'HH/LL sets review_needed_at (spec 01)' cites spec 01 for a rule spec 01 does not state; the 01 appendix says 'What sets review_needed_at: a reply that needs review, which by default means is_final OR flag > 'normal'; a corrected or struck reply; a department decline', and only 'write_dispense and write_administration pass needs_review = false'. Spec 05 ('my results … count in red when a critical is waiting'), the 02 appendix ('The department owns unreviewed results after a doctor leaves', '12 results now belong to Internal medicine') and C1 ('A correction sets review_needed_at') all presuppose the wide predicate. README: locked specs are built on and 'do not reopen'; 04 'builds on 01–03', so 01's fold rule stands. What remains is a one-sentence erratum to 04 (replace the HH/LL sentence with 01's rule: every final reply, every flagged reply, every correction and every decline sets it; HH/LL is what turns the count red) and the golden fixture the specialist proposes (a normal final CBC appears in the requester's read_to_review). Placed before Phase 0 only because change_request's fold is written there and a builder reading 04 literally would build the narrow predicate; it changes no table, no signature, and costs no build time. If it were built narrow, the later fix is a predicate change plus rebuild_record (requests is 'always recomputable from its steps and replies'), so it is not a rewrite either way.

gaps.title: Unsent drafts are invisible; a visit can lapse with the note never written
gaps.scenario: A doctor sees 50 patients, takes a phone call mid-consult, presses Back to queue on three of them, goes home. Their drafts sit in drafts with author_id; nothing lists them. The sweep moves the visits to pending and, 14 days later, lapsed. The record for those three visits contains vitals (nurse) and nothing from the doctor, and nobody was ever told. At 50 patients a day this happens weekly.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05 rule 3: 'Nothing half-written is ever in the record' and 'Back to queue keeps the drafts.' Spec 01: 'drafts entry_id · author_id · patient_id · visit_id · type · service_id · reply_to_id · data' with no read_… over it in any spec. Spec 03 sweep: 'pending ∧ away ∧ idle 14 d → lapsed'.
gaps.fix: Additive: read_drafts(organization_id) returning the caller's drafts with patient banner and visit status, an index on drafts (author_id, updated_at), and an 'unsent' count in the queue footer next to 'my results' (spec 05). The sweep stays as it is.
gaps.skeptic: Already a stated known limit and the fix is additive. 03 known limits: 'A forgotten consult with nothing out (the doctor never pressed Done, nothing holds) is swept to pending, away at 12 h, then lapses at 14 d, invisible in between.' The drafts persist per author ('Back to queue keeps the drafts'; 05 known limit 'drafts are per user') and reappear when that patient is reopened, and the queue footer's 'away (open, not present)' count already surfaces such visits at department level; so the workflow is expressible, the missing piece is a personal 'unsent' list. read_drafts(organization_id) over drafts (author_id, updated_at) and a footer count are a new function and a client change on a table that is 'outside the record … ordinary mutable', which B17 only-grows absorbs at any time. The more useful observation for Phase 0: no spec names ANY draft function — 05 rule 3 requires server-side autosave that 'survives a reload', 01 appendix says 'Committing a draft is a column-for-column copy' and machines 'write … drafts', yet 01's function list has no save_draft/read_drafts/delete_draft and 'the app never touches tables'. Those are additive too (new public functions, no core table change), so Phase 0 can start; they just need naming before the client is built.

gaps.title: Machine users cannot read, so no bidirectional analyser or LIS interface is possible
gaps.scenario: A chemistry analyser or middleware in host-query mode asks 'which tests for specimen 12345?'; an outbound HL7 v2 order feed to a reference lab needs the send-out list; an e-prescribing bridge needs the pharmacy queue. Each is a machine user that must read read_queue, read_sent_outside or the Laboratory pack's specimens. A machine holds write: only, so the bridge cannot know what to run. Only 'type the worklist on the analyser by hand, results push back' works, which a hospital lab with a track will not accept.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 02: 'A machine user holds write: actions in one department and writes only replies to requests sent there — or, in a reception department, holds read:patient, read:queue and write:visit'. 02 appendix: 'A machine user (kind = 'machine') holds only write: actions, in exactly one department, never everywhere; save_user refuses anything else' and S13: 'no read:, mark:, manage:, no everywhere.'
gaps.fix: Repeat the spec 03 kiosk pattern for service departments: a machine in a laboratory, imaging, pharmacy or ancillary department may also hold read:queue and the pack's read:<its things> in that one department. One save_user rule, one line in the S13 fixture. Writes stay replies-only; the compromised-analyser bound holds.
gaps.skeptic: Correctly placed by the specialist; the severity is overstated for this owner. 02 appendix S13 and the known limit 'Machine users are confined to replies and drafts' are deliberate (a compromised analyser login bound), and 02 'Written as rules now, built later' already schedules 'machine logins with the first analyser'. Host-query mode is speculative for a 50-patient/day IM clinic in its first two years, and when a hospital lab arrives the fix is the shape spec 03 already used for the kiosk: one more clause in save_user's machine rule (a machine in a laboratory/imaging/pharmacy/ancillary department may also hold read:queue and the pack's read:<its things> there) and one line in the S13 fixture. No table, no signature, writes stay replies-only. 'Scale unchanged' holds because nothing in the schema moves. Not before Phase 0.

gaps.title: A request from an outside doctor has no requester: the lab report cannot name who asked, and the critical goes to the typist
gaps.scenario: A GP's paper form for a CBC comes with a lab-only walk-in. A nurse types the request. The report must print 'Requested by Dr X, Green Street Practice' and the critical Hb must reach Dr X (or the lab's outside-requester phone list), not the nurse. write_request has no parameter and no data key for the outside requester: question_text is refused on a non-consult service, responsible_id must be a users row and 'nobody holds a role' outside, and data.stated_author_name exists only for source = outside entries, which write_request cannot produce. The appendix explicitly leaves this open.
gaps.where_it_breaks: 03 appendix: 'A nurse or doctor with write:request writes the request with visit_id = that visit… Who reviews an outside doctor's result is spec 01's and the laboratory pack's question.' Spec 04: 'write_request(id, patient_id, visit_id, service_id, priority, due_at, question_text, problems[], to_department_id)' and 'Refuses… a question_text on a non-consult service'. 01 appendix: 'Outside and import. These also carry data.stated_author_name'.
gaps.fix: Additive: write_request gains from_department_id (default the caller's; may name an is_outside row) and stated_requester_name (copied into data and printed on the report). requests.from_department_id then points at the outside row, so the existing read_to_review(organization_id, department_id) over from_department_id is the 'results for outside requesters' list the lab works. requester_id stays the typist.
gaps.skeptic: The convention already exists in 01; only write_request fails to expose it. 01 appendix: 'Outside and import. These also carry data.stated_author_name and data.stated_recorded_at', and entries.source has 'outside'. Spec 04 exposes source = outside only on write_result ('Outside result … source = outside, data.source_name'); write_request(id, patient_id, visit_id, service_id, priority, due_at, question_text, problems[], to_department_id) has no source or name, and 'a question_text on a non-consult service' is refused, so the GP's name has no structured home. But the workflow the specs claim (03 appendix: 'A lab-only walk-in (an outside doctor's paper request) … A nurse or doctor with write:request writes the request') runs today: the typist is requester_id = coalesce(responsible_id, author_id), the critical lands in the typist's to-review, and the paper form names the GP; 03 already says results are 'handed over at the desk'. The 03 appendix explicitly leaves 'who reviews an outside doctor's result' to 'spec 01's and the laboratory pack's question'. The fix is write_request gaining source (staff | outside) and stated_author_name exactly as write_result does — a defaulted parameter, one B17 note, no table — and read_to_review(organization_id, department_id) over from_department_id already gives the lab an outside-requesters list once from_department_id may name an is_outside row (an additive relaxation of the 'immutable copy' from the caller's department). Land it with the Laboratory pack, not before Phase 0.

gaps.title: Result review cannot be handed to a person: cover for leave is department-wide or nothing
gaps.scenario: Dr A goes on leave for three weeks (not retired). Sixty pending results sit under her requester_id. The covering doctor can only open read_to_review(department), where everyone's results are mixed; she cannot take ownership, so two doctors may review the same result or neither does. mark_routing changes the assignee at the destination, never the reviewer.
gaps.where_it_breaks: 01 appendix: 'mark_routing(request_id, assignee_id, to_department_id, priority, due_at, reason) changes who, where, how urgent or when' — 'who' is the destination's assignee; 'requests_to_review (requester_id, review_needed_at)' has no setter. 02 appendix save_user: 'returns {open_assigned, to_review} when retired_at is set so the client can say 'reassign 30; 12 results now belong to Internal medicine''.
gaps.fix: Additive parameter: mark_routing gains requester_id, recorded as a routing step {requester_id: [old, new]}; read_to_review(NULL) follows the current value. It also gives save_user's 'reassign 30' a real call per row.
gaps.skeptic: The designed cover path exists and was chosen deliberately. 02 appendix draft→final table: 'read_to_review(organization_id, department_id) — The department owns unreviewed results after a doctor leaves', over the second partial index (from_department_id, review_needed_at), for a caller holding mark:reviewed there; O8 'doctor leaving with open work: Accept, smaller: save_user returns {open_assigned, to_review}; no bulk function'; 02 'no schedules: cover is membership'; and 'retired_at may be in the future … Clearing retired_at is the one un-retire' covers a bounded leave without a column. The specialist's claim that 'reassign 30' has no call is wrong: open_assigned rows are reassigned by mark_routing(request_id, assignee_id, …), which exists; only requester_id has no setter, and 01 appendix note 'requester_id: who the reply goes back to' is a fold value, so 'two doctors review the same result' is at worst a harmless double mark_reviewed on the department list. A requester_id parameter on mark_routing recorded as a routing step is a genuine nicety and purely additive (one defaulted parameter, one changes key). core-later, low priority.

gaps.title: No cross-patient read exists and no pack may build one: registers, KPIs and returns are unreachable
gaps.scenario: A diabetes register ('every active E11 without an HbA1c in 12 months', which is also the recall list); monthly waits and DNA rates; an insurer or ministry return; an accreditation audit. Every fact needed is already in derived tables with patient_id, yet the app 'never touches tables', no read_… crosses patients, and a Reports pack is forbidden SELECT on any core table. Looping read_values per patient is the only path and it is unusable.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01: 'Functions — the app never touches tables'. Spec 06 rule 4: 'no privilege on any core table (not even a row lock)'. 01 appendix: 'Cross-patient search and cohort queries are later derived tables.' 03 appendix: 'Waits are free. seen_at − arrived_at, left counts, lapse rates… all from two tables with no clinical join' — with no function that exposes them.
gaps.fix: Additive, but decide the shape now so 06's wording is not contradicted later: either (a) a read:cohort action with read_cohort(organization_id, problem_codes[], value_code, since) over patient_problems/entry_values/patient_medications and read_visit_counts over visits/visit_steps, or (b) amend 06 rule 4 so a pack role may hold SELECT on the derived tables and visits (rebuildable, never clinically written), which makes a Reports pack possible under the existing twelve tests. (b) is smaller and keeps core out of reporting.
gaps.skeptic: Real need, already scheduled, and nothing to decide now. 01 'Written as rules now, built later: … cross-patient search (a derived table)'; 01 appendix known limits: 'Cross-patient search and cohort queries are later derived tables'; 03 appendix: waits 'come from visits and visit_steps alone'. Every fact is already in rebuildable derived tables and visits, so a register is a new read function (read_cohort over patient_problems / entry_values / patient_medications, read_visit_counts over visits / visit_steps) under a new read: action — additive, B17 only grows, no table change. The specialist's preferred option (b), amending 06 rule 4 so a pack role holds SELECT on derived tables, is the wrong direction for this owner: it reopens a locked rule ('no privilege on any core table (not even a row lock)') and the 'Postgres is the boundary' invariant for no gain, since packs may already call every public read_… function (06: 'EXECUTE on … every public read_… and mark_…'). Option (a) contradicts nothing later, so the shape need not be fixed before Phase 0. The IM clinic will want a diabetes recall list inside a year, so put read_cohort first in the core-later queue; a Reports pack then sits on top of it.

gaps.title: The read audit exists but nothing returns it
gaps.scenario: A patient asks who opened their chart (GDPR art. 15, HIPAA accounting); a privacy officer investigates a staff member looking up a colleague. record_reads holds the answer; no function reads it, so the answer needs a database console.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 02: 'record_reads organization_id · user_id · patient_id · read_at' and the read_… list 'read_settings_changes (manage:organization)' with no reader of record_reads; 02 appendix: 'so the audit shows only people'.
gaps.fix: Additive: read_record_reads(patient_id) returning rows with user name and read_at under manage:organization (later also for the patient's own kind through patient_access).
gaps.skeptic: Accurate observation, additive fix. Spec 02 lists record_reads (organization_id · user_id · patient_id · read_at, insert-only, indexed (user_id, patient_id, read_at desc) in the appendix) and read_settings_changes (manage:organization) but no reader over record_reads; 02 'built later' already names 'restricted records and record_reads.reason_text'. A GDPR/HIPAA accounting is a compliance duty, not a clinical workflow, and for a small clinic the console answers it until read_record_reads(patient_id) under manage:organization is added — a new function, no table, no signature change. Ship it alongside the settings-history page, after Phase 0.

gaps.title: Banner alerts (code status, isolation, safeguarding, interpreter) have no type and no slot
gaps.scenario: DNACPR on a ward; MRSA isolation; a violent-patient warning; pregnancy; 'hard of hearing, bring an interpreter'. These must be on the banner of every screen. Core's banner shows allergies only, core has no alert type ('nine, no more'), and a pack can ship an alert type with a list but cannot draw it in the banner because the banner has no slot; the workaround, a problem coded Z66, sits in the problems column where it is not seen.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05 visit: 'banner: name · age/sex · record number · ⚠ allergies (always) · died · open requests'. Spec 04: 'Nine types, no more in core'. Spec 06 known limits: 'a pack cannot add a column to a core settings page beyond the one servicesColumns slot' — and the banner has no slot at all.
gaps.fix: Client-only: a bannerItems slot in the renderer registry (renderers[type].Banner), fed by the pack's own <key>_read_… of its list. An admissions or safety pack then ships alert as a type with a patient_alerts list; no server change.
gaps.skeptic: Expressible today, and the ward case arrives with a pack anyway. Spec 05's visit screen shows the RECORD column ('problems (✓ ✎ ✕ + add)') on every visit screen beside the banner, so a coded problem (Z66 DNACPR, Z22 carrier, pregnancy, safeguarding) is always in view — the specialist's 'sits in the problems column where it is not seen' is not what 05 draws; 'interpreter' is 03's additive language_name. A pack may already ship an alert type with a patient_alerts list under 06 (a list with a pure updater, like pregnancies) and render its own cards. What is missing is only a client slot: renderers[type].Banner (or bannerItems) next to { Card, Full, Editor } in 05's registry so a pack type can draw in the banner — client-only, no server change, no locked rule touched (06's known limit is about settings pages). Not blocking a hospital: wards are 'admissions pack' territory in 05, and a ward's DNACPR line lands when that pack and this slot ship together.

gaps.title: A bookings pack cannot plug into reception
gaps.scenario: An IM clinic with 50 booked patients a day. The desk needs today's list with Here on each row and a DNA mark on those who never arrive. Spec 03 correctly keeps bookings out of visits, but the reception screen is core's and packs ship screens for their own department types only, so the bookings pack would have to invent a second desk department type that duplicates reception.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05: '1 · Reception (department type reception) The search box is the screen.' Spec 06: 'screens per department type' and 'a pack cannot add a column to a core settings page beyond the one servicesColumns slot'. Spec 03: 'a bookings pack whose bookings point at the visit they became; a no-show is a booking that never became a visit.'
gaps.fix: Client-only: a receptionPanels slot (like servicesColumns) above the merged queue, fed by the pack's bookings_read_day(department_id); its Here calls core's open_visit with the booking's patient and department. No server change.
gaps.skeptic: The specs already answer this and the answer is a pack screen, not a core slot. 03 'built later': 'a bookings pack whose bookings point at the visit they became; a no-show is a booking that never became a visit'; 03 appendix Y1: 'no pack executes a visit function; order inside a band is arrival, slot order is the pack screen's'; boundary 4: 'the client calls open_visit as the desk user and hands the id to the pack'; and 'A kiosk, a wall board, a bookings pack and admissions need no ALTER.' Under 06 rule 1 the bookings pack ships a department type (a diary desk), the practice makes one, served_departments(diary, NULL) lets its receptionist's write:visit pass on every clinic, and its day list's Here calls core's open_visit; the receptionist has Reception and the diary one keystroke apart in the shell. That is not 'duplicating reception' (search + queue versus a day list). A receptionPanels slot above the merged queue is a later client-only nicety; nothing in Phase 0 depends on it. Corrected belongs: pack.

gaps.title: Courses and tapers: a prescription cannot start later or end by itself, so lists rot
gaps.scenario: Prednisolone 40→30→20→10 mg over four weeks; nitrofurantoin for five days; 'start warfarin tomorrow'. Clinical time may not be in the future and there is no starts_on, so a taper is instructions_text; duration_days is recorded but nothing ends the row, so a month later the medication list still shows the antibiotic as active and the allergy/interaction underline matches against it. Reconciliation at every follow-up pays for this.
gaps.where_it_breaks: 01 appendix: 'Clinical time. occurred_at <= recorded_at + 5 minutes. Future clinical time belongs in due_at.' Spec 04: 'write_prescription(… duration_days, quantity, repeats, instructions_text …)' with no starts_on; 'stop: the row gets stopped_on' is a manual act; patient_medications 'status (active | stopped)'.
gaps.fix: Additive keys: write_prescription gains starts_on (partial date, default today) into data; the updater stores patient_medications.starts_on and ends_on = starts_on + duration_days (pure, no clock); read_record.medications marks ends_on < today as 'course ended' at read time. A taper is N start entries in one set with stepping starts_on. No new status.
gaps.skeptic: Awkward but expressible, and the fix is additive. Spec 04 records duration_days, quantity, repeats and instructions_text on the entry; 'start tomorrow' and a taper are instructions_text or N start entries in one write_set (04 known limit: 'a regimen is N entries in one set'); 04 rule 6 makes reconciliation at follow-up the designed act ('Reviewed is a fact you write, per list, per Done'), and the ✓ ✎ ✕ marks on the medication column are one keystroke each. patient_medications carries started_on and stopped_on but not duration_days, and its updater is pure ('no clock'), so 'course ended' cannot be computed there; it can be computed at read time in read_record once duration_days (or ends_on = starts_on + duration_days) is a nullable column on a table that is 'deletable and rebuildable' — the cheapest kind of migration in this design. starts_on as a partial date in data is a defaulted parameter. No new status, no locked rule touched (future clinical time stays in due_at). core-later, bundle with the Pharmacy pack.

gaps.title: Patient-reported and outside medications cannot be recorded without claiming to have prescribed them
gaps.scenario: Admission or first-visit reconciliation: the patient takes amlodipine from another clinic and ibuprofen over the counter. The only way onto patient_medications is write_prescription(start), which stamps the caller as prescriber_id and prints on a script. Recording 'reported as taking' and 'I prescribed' as the same act is a medicolegal and a clinical error (the ward doctor now owns a drug they never chose).
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04: 'write_prescription(id, patient_id, visit_id, action, medication_id, drug {…}, …)' with no source; 'patient_medications … prescriber_id'. Spec 01 sources '(staff | patient | machine | outside | import)' and 01 appendix 'Outside and import. These also carry data.stated_author_name' apply only to entries a function can mark outside, which write_prescription cannot.
gaps.fix: Additive: write_prescription gains source (staff | outside | patient) and stated_prescriber_name; patient_medications.prescriber_id becomes nullable beside a prescriber_name; the list prints 'reported' on source ≠ staff rows. Reconciliation is then one set of start(source = outside)/stop/change plus a list_review.
gaps.skeptic: Same root as the outside-requester gap: the convention exists in 01 (entries.source 'patient | outside'; 'Outside and import … carry data.stated_author_name') and write_prescription does not expose it. For the first target it is expressible now: without a Pharmacy pack a start is 'a paper script: no request, no queue', the recorder simply does not print it and instructions_text says 'patient-reported, from Dr X'; prescriber_id = recorder is a medico-legal nuance, not a block. The sharper problem the specialist did not name is what makes this necessary with the Pharmacy pack: 'A prescription is a request exactly when the organization has a live dispense service the caller's department is served by', so recording a home amlodipine would send a dispensing request to Pharmacy, which must decline it with a not_done reply. The fix is write_prescription gaining source (staff | outside | patient) and stated_prescriber_name, source ≠ staff writing no request row, prescriber_id nullable beside prescriber_name on a rebuildable derived table — additive, one B17 note. It must land no later than the Pharmacy pack, but Phase 0 does not wait for it.

gaps.title: Stopping a drug closes only the dispensing request; a ward administration request keeps it due
gaps.scenario: On a ward the same prescription is two requests: dispense to Pharmacy and administer to the ward ('Supply plus administer is two requests'). The doctor stops the drug. Spec 04's stop closes the dispensing request only; the ward's administration request stays open and the nurse's due list keeps showing the dose. The admissions pack cannot close it either: its role holds no mark:cancelled, so it must write a final not_done reply of its own type from after_write, seconds later, to stop a dose that should never be offered.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 prescription: 'stop: the row gets stopped_on, stop_reason_text, status = stopped, and the row's open dispensing request, if any, is closed done with the reason.' 01 appendix: 'One request, one destination. Supply plus administer is two requests.' Spec 02: the pack user's role holds 'mark:held and actions of its own types and steps only'.
gaps.fix: Widen the spec 04 stop rule: close every open request whose entry is this prescription or whose data.medication_id names this row, with the reason. One query inside write_prescription, no schema. The convention 'a pack request that follows a medication carries data.medication_id' goes into 06.
gaps.skeptic: Correct reading of the text, wrong severity, and the pack can already close it.
