Spec 04 stop closes 'the row's open dispensing request, if any'; 01 appendix: 'A second destination is a second request entry' and 'Supply plus administer is two requests'; inpatient dose charts are 01 'built later'. Today the requester (a ward doctor holds doctor in the ward, so mark:cancelled on to_department_id passes) cancels the administration request with the stop reason in a second call; and an admissions pack's after_write sees the stop entry and may close its own administration request with a final not_done reply of its own reply type (allowed: a pack 'never writes a core type', but this is its type), which the fold turns into cancelled — 'seconds later' is the accepted after-write latency (06 known limits). Widening the stop rule to 'every open request whose data.medication_id names this row' is one query inside write_prescription plus a data convention line in 06: additive body change, no schema. Land it with the admissions pack.

gaps.title: Co-signature: the appendix and spec 04 disagree, and a note cannot show whether it was countersigned
gaps.scenario: A resident writes a history and physical that the attending must attest. The appendix says the note itself is a request; spec 04 gives note no request behaviour and write_note no service. What is expressible is a set {note, request to a 'Co-signature' service with reply_type note} linked only by written_with_id, and the attending answering with a final consult_reply. Nobody reading the note card can see it is unsigned, and a teaching hospital's attestation report has nothing to query.
gaps.where_it_breaks: 01 appendix: 'A trainee note is itself a request to the Co-signature service.' Spec 04 note row: behaviours 'reply (kind consult_reply) · values · files' and 'write_note(id, patient_id, visit_id, kind, text, fields, problems[], reply_to_id, is_final, files[])' with no service_id; 'Any other kind refuses reply_to_id'.
gaps.fix: State the set convention in spec 04 (a trainee note is written in one set with a request to a Co-signature service; the attending's final consult_reply closes it) and have read_record's note card carry the sibling request's step via written_with_id (one join). No columns.
gaps.skeptic: The disagreement is one loose sentence and the set convention is already the design. 01 appendix C14: 'Accept as two written conventions. No cosigned_at'; rejected: 'cosigned_at, a needs_review column … Conventions plus review_needed_at cover these needs without claiming a review that never happened'; known limit: 'No co-signature column'. Spec 04 gives note no request behaviour and no service_id, so 'a trainee note is itself a request' must be read as 'is written in one set with a request to a Co-signature service' — expressible today via write_set with written_with_id, the attending answering with a final consult_reply note. The second convention, 'A trainee consult reply is a preliminary reply, and the attending writes the final', works as written (is_final false, then a final reply). Visibility is better than the specialist says: 05 draws 'one card per thread', so the open Co-signature request is its own card beside the note, and read_record.open_requests lists it. What is left is a sentence in 04 stating the set convention and, optionally, read_record's note card carrying the sibling request's step via written_with_id — a read-shape addition, no columns. Teaching-hospital attestation reporting is the cross-patient gap, not this one. core-later.

gaps.title: A send-out request can never be answered
gaps.scenario: An internal-medicine clinic with no lab sends every FBC and HbA1c to a reference laboratory (services.department_id NULL, an outside department created on first use). The PDF comes back. Nobody holds write:result in an outside department, so the result cannot be written as the reply; the designed route files it as an unsolicited outside result plus a second 'Review result' request, and the original send-out stays open in read_sent_outside forever or is cancelled with an invented reason. The same happens to a GP letter's reply, an outside referral's clinic letter and an outside consult. Twelve of the thirty stress scenarios that touch the outside world (GP letter, shared care, patient message, translated document) run into this gate.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 result: 'Caller must hold write:result in the request's to_department_id.' Spec 02: 'outside (created on first use; nobody holds a role there)' and 'read:queue also passes on an outside department for anyone holding it in the organization' — only read:queue widens. Spec 04 outside result: 'The client writes it in a set with a request to the clinician's department (Review result).' Spec 03 read_sent_outside lists 'open requests … to an is_outside destination' with nothing that closes them.
gaps.fix: One clause in require_access, mirroring the read:queue widening: write:result (and mark:<step> for the requester's own routing) passes on an is_outside to_department_id for anyone holding it anywhere in the organization. The reply is written with source = outside, data.stated_author_name, data.stated_recorded_at and files[]; the fold closes the send-out and review_needed_at fires as for any final reply, so 'Review result' is no longer needed. It is a gate rule and a B16 tenant-matrix expectation, both written in Phase 0; deciding it now avoids amending two locked specs later.
gaps.skeptic: Confirmed against the text. Spec 04 result: 'Caller must hold write:result in the request's to_department_id'; spec 02 appendix line 70: outside rows are created by write_request on first use and 'nobody holds a role there (trigger on user_roles)'; spec 02 appendix line 114: 'Two widenings, both narrow' and only read:queue reaches an is_outside department. So a request whose destination is_outside — the exact route spec 02 O14 (send-out queue), spec 03 read_sent_outside and spec 01 appendix Y5 ('Outside departments are created on first use') claim to serve — has no legal reply. The only in-rule routes are (a) file the PDF as an unsolicited result plus a 'Review result' request and cancel the send-out with a reason that is false, or (b) never use is_outside at all and model the reference lab as an inside ancillary department staffed by a filing clerk. Route (b) works and I would tell the first clinic to do it, which is why this is not a table change; but it abandons read_sent_outside for its primary purpose and leaves referral letters, GP letters and outside consults, which have no inside handler, with no close at all. The first target sends HbA1c and TSH out daily, so it is hit on day one. The fix is one clause in require_access (write:result, and the requester's own cancel/routing, pass on an is_outside to_department_id — either for anyone holding the action in the organization, mirroring read:queue, or narrower: for holders in the request's from_department_id) plus one sentence in write_result allowing source = outside with stated_author_name / stated_recorded_at on a reply. It is not a rewrite risk; it stays core-before-phase-0 because the gate and the outside-department trigger are both migration-one objects, the clause costs one line while they are being written, and deferring it means shipping a gate that makes the first clinic's daily workflow unclosable until two locked specs are amended.

gaps.title: No always-visible alert on the core banner
gaps.scenario: A DNACPR decision, an advance directive, MRSA status, a safeguarding flag, 'anticoagulated', 'research participant', 'interpreter needed'. A palliative or admissions pack writes its own type with a list and a signed file, but the patient then attends the core internal-medicine clinic screen, whose banner shows allergies only; the clinician sees the decision only by scrolling the timeline or opening the pack's screen. The workaround inside the rules is a second entry, a problem row (icd10/snomed 'not for resuscitation'), which lands in the RECORD column, not the banner. The same absence of slots hits the reception screen (a bookings pack cannot show today's appointments on the core Reception screen) and core-type rendering (an emergency pack's NEWS2 score cannot be drawn on the core vitals card; it lives on a second card).
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05 visit screen: 'banner: name · age/sex · record number · ⚠ allergies (always) · died · open requests'. Spec 04 read_record shape has no alerts key. Spec 05 rule 4: 'a pack may register a richer renderer for its own types'. Spec 06: exports '{ key, departmentScreens, renderers, servicesColumns, presetFragment, actions }' and known limit 'a pack cannot add a column to a core settings page beyond the one servicesColumns slot'.
gaps.fix: Smallest: the core banner also draws read_record.problems whose code is in a client alertCodes set that a pack's index may extend (alerts: [codes]); the pack writes its own type and the problem row in one write_set. Cleaner once needed: a tenth core type alert with list patient_alerts (kind, code, name, text, review_on, status active | ended) returned as read_record.alerts and drawn beside allergies. Both are additive; read_record's returned shape may grow.
gaps.skeptic: The specialist's own text concedes the workaround lands 'in the RECORD column, not the banner' — and spec 05's visit screen shows the RECORD column (problems, medications, allergies) at all times beside TODAY, not in the scrolling timeline. A DNACPR or MRSA problem row (write_problem with icd10:Z66 or a SNOMED code) is therefore visible on every core visit open without scrolling; read_record.problems already returns it. What is missing is only placement: the banner and the queue row's ⚠ draw allergies alone. That is a client rule in src/core (draw problems whose code is in an alert-code set beside allergies), needs no table, no function and no change to read_record's shape, and belongs with the client build, not with Phase 0 migrations. A tenth 'alert' type is speculative structure until a real pack shows the problem row is insufficient. The NEWS2 case is not a gap: spec 04 says 'a paediatrics or emergency pack may write flags' and a pack renders its own type. The bookings-on-reception case is a client slot decided when the bookings pack is specced (spec 03 built-later).

gaps.title: Core write functions take no extension key: data is open, the funnels are closed
gaps.scenario: A sepsis pathway (pack) fires six requests from a template and wants each request card to carry 'sepsis pathway, hour 1'; a study id on a result; a care-plan id on a prescription; a lot number on a core administration reply. write_request shapes data entirely from its parameters; the only link list is problems[]; a request added after the pathway's first Done shares no written_with_id. Only note.fields is open. A pack can keep a side table of core ids, but then read_record cards cannot say what they belong to.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04: 'write_request(id, patient_id, visit_id, service_id, priority, due_at, question_text, problems[], to_department_id)' and 'data service {…} · priority · due_at · question_text · problems[]'; likewise write_result, write_prescription, write_vitals, write_problem, write_allergy. Spec 01 rule 1: 'A new fact is a key in data' — true of the spine, unreachable through eight of the nine core funnels. Spec 04 note: 'fields is the filled form of a structured template' is the one open door.
gaps.fix: One optional parameter on every core write function, in the shape problems[] already has: links[] = [{id, type, display_line}] pointing at entries of the same patient (checked like replaces_id, stored at data.links[], copied self-contained). The card renders 'part of ‹display_line›'. Signatures grow by one defaulted parameter; no table changes. Until then, written_with_id and a pack-side link table cover the common case.
gaps.skeptic: Every cited case has a home the specs already imply. A sepsis pathway's six requests come from a template expanded 'to N write_request calls inside one write_set' (spec 04), so they share written_with_id; and data.problems[] = [{id, code, name}] (spec 01 appendix) links each request to the 'Sepsis' problem row, whose name the card can show — that is the clinical link, and it survives a request added after the first Done. A study id or lot number belongs on the pack's own type (write_administration is a pack type with open data) or in a pack table keyed by entry id (spec 06 rule 5). A generic links[] on all nine core functions is exactly the speculative structure the owner rejects. If a real pack ever needs a core card to say 'part of X', an overload with one defaulted parameter is additive under 'signatures only grow' (the old line stays; a new one is gained). Nothing here touches a table or delays Phase 0.

gaps.title: Packs cannot ship global codes
gaps.scenario: The obstetrics pack needs fundal height and per-fetus heart rates (twin A / twin B as two codes), paediatrics needs head circumference and weight-for-age z, cardiology QTc. None is in the core LOINC vitals set. Each organization's preset mints a different local: code at setup, so the pack's read_values must first find the organization's code by name, and two organizations' exports disagree on the same measurement.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 02: 'A global codes row (organization_id IS NULL) is written only by a _core_ migration'. Spec 06 registry rows a pack ships: 'packs · entry_types · department_types · actions · roles + role_actions' — codes is absent. Spec 01: 'Values' codes must exist in codes (they trend)'.
gaps.fix: An additive nullable codes.pack; a pack migration may insert global codes rows carrying its key under the same permanent, never-reused rule; codes joins the registry list of spec 06 test 2. _core_ keeps the vitals set.
gaps.skeptic: The rule is real: spec 02 'A global codes row (organization_id IS NULL) is written only by a _core_ migration', spec 06's registry list omits codes, and B11 would count a pack-inserted codes row as core drift; there is also no save_code in spec 02's function list ('a codes page' is built later), so a pack's preset fragment cannot mint organization-own codes either. But the fix is additive twice over: either _core_ ships the LOINC rows a pack needs as a data migration (LOINC is universal and core already owns the vitals set — no rule changes), or codes.pack is added as a nullable column and codes joins the registry list in spec 06 test 2. The specialist's worry that 'two organizations' exports disagree' does not arise when the code string (loinc:11881-0) ships with the pack, whoever inserts the row. The first pack that needs a non-core trending code (Obstetrics, Paediatrics, Cardiology's QTc) is not in the first two years of an internal-medicine clinic; Laboratory's analytes are the one near-term case and a _core_ data migration covers them. Decide the mechanism with the first pack that needs it.

gaps.title: Identifier strings have no place in the data key rule
gaps.scenario: A vaccine lot number, an implant serial, a blood unit number, a specimen accession number, a device UDI. None is text, a name, a code, a choice or a date, so the fixture scan has no category for them, and the 'one generic de-identification function' that relies on the key rule would keep an implant serial, which is unique to one person. The existing precedent {specimen_no} also breaks the no-abbreviations rule.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01 appendix conventions: 'Every other string is a code, a choice or a date' (CI 22 scans every fixture). Spec 01 Naming: 'No abbreviations except id, mime, url'. Spec 06: 'a specimen is a step's changes {specimen_no}'. Spec 01 appendix: 'De-identification is one generic function, because of the key rule'.
gaps.fix: Add one suffix now: _number for identifier strings (lot_number, serial_number, unit_number, specimen_number, accession_number); the de-identifier drops *_number with *_text and *_name; rename specimen_no. It is the Phase 0 fixture-scan rule, not a table.
gaps.skeptic: The rule as written (spec 01 appendix line 104: 'Every other string is a code, a choice or a date', scanned on golden fixtures) does not fit a lot number, a serial or an accession number, and the de-identifier (line 486) is built later, not in Phase 0. But no core type carries such a string: the nine types' data keys are service, values, text/_text, _name, codes, choices and dates, and source_key is a column, not data. The first identifier string enters the record with the Laboratory pack (specimen in request_steps.changes, which is not entries.data) or the Pharmacy pack (a lot number on a dispense). Adding a _number suffix to the allowed set is one line in the scan and one line in the naming list when that pack is specced — additive, no fixture rewrite. Two small text fixes are worth making in passing rather than as a Phase 0 item: spec 06's worked Laboratory example and spec 01 appendix lines 163 and 286 say specimen_no, which breaks spec 01's 'No abbreviations except id, mime, url'; rename to specimen_number in the Laboratory pack spec.

gaps.title: A file cannot be added to an existing entry
gaps.scenario: Consent signed today, the scanned form arrives tomorrow; a wound photo for yesterday's note; the GP's signed letter returned by post; an Arabic translation of a discharge letter. entry_files rows are written with the entry. The only routes are a replacement entry, whose display line says 'Corrected: …' for something that is not a correction, or a new note that clutters the timeline and links to nothing.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01: 'entry_files entry_id · position · path | url · mime · name' under 'Insert-only; a trigger refuses update and delete'; files arrive only through write_note(…, files[]) and write_result(…, files[]); no write_entry_file exists; display_line is ''Corrected: …' when it replaces a final entry'.
gaps.fix: write_entry_file(entry_id, position, path | url, mime, name): appends a row (position = max + 1) to a live, unreplaced entry of the same patient, gated write:<type> in the entry's department. Rows are only ever added, so permanence and the bucket rules hold; the card shows the file count.
gaps.skeptic: The convention is already implied by spec 01's first sentence: the record is a list of entries, so a document that arrives is an entry. A scanned consent form arriving tomorrow is write_note(kind = other or procedure, occurred_at backdated to the signing, text 'Signed consent, colonoscopy', files[], problems[]) — occurred_at is clinical time and may precede recorded_at (appendix line 85); a wound photo for yesterday's visit is the same with visit_id set (a note into an ended visit of the same patient succeeds, spec 03 boundary 1); the GP's returned signed letter is the reply to the letter's request once gap 1 is fixed. None of these is a 'correction', so no replacement entry is needed, and a card on the timeline for a document that arrived is not clutter — it is the audit trail. write_entry_file(entry_id, position, …) would be an additive new function that keeps entry_files insert-only, and can land if a real pack shows the entry-per-document convention is insufficient. Not a Phase 0 item.

gaps.title: The frequency set lacks continuous, and packs cannot contribute to a core list
gaps.scenario: A heparin infusion at 1000 U/h over hours, or maintenance fluids, must appear in patient_medications because every department of the hospital reads that list. write_prescription refuses a frequency outside the core set, and a ward pack's own infusion type cannot update the core list: its updater is dispatched as <pack>.update_patient_medications, which holds no privilege on the table. Rate changes and stop are expressible as non-final replies to the ward administration request; the running state is a pack list; the point-in-time occurred_at is fine because start and stop are two acts.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 prescription: 'Refuses … a frequency outside the core set (OD BD TDS QDS q4h q6h q8h q12h weekly monthly PRN once stat)'. Spec 02 dispatch: 'format('%I.%I', coalesce(entry_types.pack, 'core'), 'update_' || list)'. Spec 06: 'no privilege on any core table'.
gaps.fix: Add continuous to the core frequency set (one value in a CHECK list); the rate stays in instructions_text until structured sigs ship; the infusion's running rate is the latest non-final reply.
gaps.skeptic: The omission is real for a ward and irrelevant for the first target: no outpatient internal-medicine prescription is 'continuous'. Spec 01 lists 'inpatient dose charts (rule 6)' and spec 04 'hold/resume on a medication (inpatient)' as written-now-built-later, so the ward case is an acknowledged later step, and the running rate as 'the latest non-final reply' is rule 6 as written. Adding continuous is one value in write_prescription's refusal list and, if patient_medications.frequency is constrained, one ADD VALUE or CHECK change on a derived, rebuildable table — additive, landing with the pack that first writes an infusion. The second half ('packs cannot contribute to a core list') is by design (spec 02 dispatch names coalesce(entry_types.pack, 'core')) and correct: the medications list has one writer, the core prescription type, which is exactly why every department can trust it.

gaps.title: Standing orders: the due_at roll-forward has no named source
gaps.scenario: Weekly FBC on clozapine, monthly B12 injection, daily home BP. One request with non-final replies is the designed shape and read_queue(is_upcoming) shows it, but 'rolled forward by repeated acts' names no rule for by how much, so change_request cannot be written; and the lab bench sees a standing order in step replied rather than awaiting. A finite series (6 × weekly) is already clean: N requests in one write_set with future due_at.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01 appendix requests: 'due_at timestamptz not null default = request time; 'infinity' = as needed (PRN); rolled forward by repeated acts'. Spec 01 appendix: 'Home monitoring is a standing request whose readings are non-final replies'.
gaps.fix: A non-final reply may carry data.next_due_at; change_request sets requests.due_at := coalesce(reply.data.next_due_at, due_at). The client or pack computes it from the request's data.frequency, so change_request never parses frequencies. Name the key before change_request is written in Phase 0, but it is a function rule, not a table.
gaps.skeptic: The source exists already: mark_routing(request_id, assignee_id, to_department_id, priority, due_at, reason) 'changes who, where, how urgent or when' (spec 01 appendix line 283), and a pack role holds EXECUTE on every public mark_… (spec 06), so a ward or pharmacy wrapper writes the non-final reply and calls mark_routing with the next due_at in the same function. The appendix's 'rolled forward by repeated acts' (line 129) is a description of the outcome, not an instruction to change_request; Phase 0 can write change_request to leave due_at alone on a reply, which is the simplest reading and what the fold rule ('always recomputable from its steps and replies') already implies, since a routing step records {due_at}. A data.next_due_at key that change_request honours is a one-line convenience to add when inpatient dose charts ship (spec 01 built-later). The lab-bench bucket for a standing order is the Laboratory pack's own screen rule. Nothing here is a Phase 0 decision.

gaps.title: Prefetch turns the read audit into noise
gaps.scenario: A nurse opens the Internal Medicine queue at 08:00. Spec 05 prefetches `read_record` for the 30 present patients. The audit now says she opened 30 charts, including the colleague-who-is-a-patient she never looked at. When the privacy officer investigates a snooping complaint, every staff member who opened the queue that day is a hit and the log proves nothing. The one purpose of `record_reads` — showing who looked at whom — is defeated on day one.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05, Cross-cutting: "**Prefetch the day.** Opening a queue calls `read_record` for everyone present (the 30 open charts of a clinic are a few megabytes); a patient opens with no round trip." against spec 02, Access: "**Record reads:** `read_record` inserts a `record_reads` row; the other record reads raise `record_not_open` without one in the last 12 hours."
gaps.fix: Amend 05 before the first `record_reads` row exists, so a row always means "this person's screen showed this chart": the client prefetches only the pinned patient and the next patient in band order (the one `Done → Next` will open), and every other chart opens on selection with one round trip (well inside 300 ms from a near region). No table or signature changes; the rule changes, and changing it after go-live leaves the early audit unreadable.
gaps.skeptic: Spec 05 Cross-cutting "Opening a queue calls `read_record` for everyone present" collides head-on with spec 02 Access "`read_record` inserts a `record_reads` row", whose stated purpose (02 appendix: "so the audit shows only people"; 02 decisions #8: "every human read of a patient one attributable row") is defeated. It is worse than noise: the prefetch also opens the 12-hour `record_not_open` window on all 30 charts, so every later `read_entries`/`read_entry_file` on any queued patient passes silently for the rest of the shift. And spec 03's appendix section k already lists "prefetching every present record" among the draft's rejections (beside "`read_queue` returning both halves", which 05 also re-adopts), so this is a contradiction between two locked specs, not a design choice. The specialist's fix is right: prefetch the pinned patient and the next in band order, open everything else on selection; the budget line "Chart open < 300 ms (from prefetch)" becomes "from one call". Belongs corrected: it touches no table, no signature and no Phase 0 migration; it is a one-paragraph amendment to 05 that must land before `src/core`'s queue screen is written (after Phase 0) and before the first `record_reads` row exists. It does not gate a migration, so it is not core-before-phase-0.

gaps.title: No sealed departments: sexual health, psychiatry and substance-use entries are visible to every role holder
gaps.scenario: A hospital has a GUM clinic and a psychiatry department. A cardiology nurse with `read:record` opens a patient's chart and sees the psychiatry notes, the HIV viral-load request in `open_requests`, and antiretrovirals in the medication list. UK GUM confidentiality rules and US 42 CFR Part 2 forbid this; the hospital cannot host those services on the system. Proxies for adolescents (Gillick) hit the same wall.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01: "Every department reads and writes the same record." Spec 04 `read_record`: "open_requests requests rows with the entry's display_line, service name, step, is_holding · entries the last 30 timeline cards". Spec 02 gate: "holding the action through a role in that department or everywhere" — nothing narrows by the entry's `department_id`.
gaps.fix: Additive settings column `departments.is_sealed`. `read_record`, `read_entries`, `read_entry`, `read_values`, `read_entry_file` and the prefetch exclude entries whose `department_id` is sealed unless the caller holds a role in that department; problem rows follow `latest_entry_id → entries.department_id`. State the drug-safety exception now: `patient_allergies` and `patient_medications` are never sealed (the drug shows, the department name renders as "sealed"). `patient_access` inherits the same filter for proxies. No new table, no signature change, but the rule must be written before the Psychiatry and Sexual-health packs are specced.
gaps.skeptic: Spec 01 "Every department reads and writes the same record" is the design's deliberate stance and its safety argument (the Psychiatry allergy shows in Cardiology). The shape UK GUM law actually demands, a separate record, the system already offers as a separate organization (01: "no cross-organization record", scale-out is "database per organization"): a GUM clinic or a 42 CFR Part 2 program runs as its own organization on day one with no spec change. Those are service-specific statutes, not "a hospital cannot run"; neither Psychiatry nor Sexual-health is among the named packs; "blocks-a-hospital" is overstated. If a sealed department inside one record is ever wanted, the specialist's own fix shows it is additive: `departments.is_sealed` plus a filter in `read_record`/`read_entries`/`read_entry`/`read_values`/`read_entry_file`, list rows through `latest_entry_id → entries.department_id`, no signature change; nothing in Phase 0 forecloses it. Write nothing now.

gaps.title: No restricted patient and no break-glass
gaps.scenario: A staff member is admitted; a well-known patient attends; a domestic-abuse victim asks that her record be limited. Any of 400 role holders can open the chart silently. The spec lists `is_restricted` and `record_reads.reason_text` as built later, but the rule that decides who passes silently is unwritten, and without it the later migration will be argued from scratch.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 02 Access: "**The gate** passes when the caller is an unretired … users row of the organization holding the action through a role in that department or everywhere"; spec 02 built-later: "restricted records and `record_reads.reason_text`"; spec 03 additive list: "`is_restricted`".
gaps.fix: Write the rule now, build with the additive columns: `patients.is_restricted` and `record_reads.reason_text`. `require_access` already takes `patient_id`, so no signature changes. A read of a restricted patient passes silently when the caller's department has an open visit for the patient or an open request from or to it (the care relationship is derivable from `visits` and `requests`); otherwise `read_record(patient_id, reason_text)` (signatures only grow) is required, the row carries the reason, and the Organization page lists reads-with-reason. Setting `is_restricted` is `write:patient` at the desk, so it needs no MFA.
gaps.skeptic: Already a stated later item twice: spec 02 built-later "restricted records and `record_reads.reason_text`" and spec 03's additive list "`is_restricted`". Both are nullable columns, `require_access` already takes `patient_id`, and `read_record` may grow a `reason_text` under "signatures only grow", so no rewrite follows from building without it. The primary control for a staff-member-as-patient in a 400-user hospital is the read audit, which exists once gap 1 is fixed and which regulators accept; break-glass is common, not mandated. Severity is "awkward" at hospital scale and nothing at the first target. One caution on the specialist's rule: derive the care relationship from `requests` (from/to department) and the caller's department's open visit that `read_record` already returns; do not add visit joins to the other record reads (03 boundary rule 1: "no record read takes or joins a visit").

gaps.title: Critical results have a flag but no clock: nothing escalates, and no pack can
gaps.scenario: A potassium of 6.8 is released at 17:10 on a Friday. `review_needed_at` is set; the requester has gone home; the red count sits in a footer nobody is looking at until Monday. Accreditation (Joint Commission NPSG.02.03.01, UK equivalents) requires a timed closed loop: notify a responsible clinician within a defined interval and document the read-back. A notification pack cannot do it: it reacts to entries at write time only and has no cron.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 result: "`HH`/`LL` sets `review_needed_at` (spec 01)"; spec 05 queue footer: "**my results** (`read_to_review`, count in red when a critical is waiting)"; spec 06: "A pack reacts to **entries only, never to steps**"; spec 02: pack roles hold "no USAGE on another schema (`net`, `extensions`, `vault`, `storage`, `auth`, `cron`, `realtime`, another pack)". Spec 01 appendix claims "The age of `review_needed_at` gives escalation … with no new schema" — but nothing consumes the age.
gaps.fix: One core job `core.escalate_reviews()` in B11's `cron.job` set (every 5 min): for every request with `review_needed_at` older than a constant and `reply_flag` in (HH, LL), signal `queue:<from_department_id>`; `read_to_review` rows already carry `review_needed_at`, so the footer shows the oldest age. The Laboratory pack ships the closed-loop step `notified` (`ADD VALUE`) with `changes {to_user_id, read_back}` so the phone call is a `request_steps` row. Declare now, as built-later, a third reaction `packs.is_called_on_schedule → <pack>.every_minute(organization_id)` so a paging pack is an additive column, not a rewrite of the two-reaction rule.
gaps.skeptic: The accreditation loop (NPSG.02.03.01: the lab reports a critical to a responsible clinician within a defined time, read-back documented) is a lab-side act at release, when the bench already knows the flag is HH/LL (04: "`flag` is computed once"). The Laboratory pack can express it today under spec 06: a `notified` step (`ADD VALUE`) with `changes {to_user_id, read_back}` taken before release, or a row in its own `laboratory.critical_calls`. Trap in the specialist's fix: a `notified` step after the final reply moves `step` off `done` and the generated `status` back to open (01 appendix: "anything else → open"), so the step goes before release or in the pack's table. The "no pack can" claim is therefore wrong for the part regulators require. What no pack can do is timed re-notification of a requester who went home; that is "cover is membership" (02) plus `read_to_review(organization_id, department_id)` whose rows already carry `review_needed_at`, so the department's oldest critical is a client sort now. If an automatic nudge is ever wanted it is one core cron job added to B11's `cron.job` list (a release, additive), not a third pack reaction; `is_called_on_schedule` is speculative structure and must not be declared now.

gaps.title: Rule 4 is right to write, wrong to forget: warning overrides leave no trace
gaps.scenario: The screen underlines amoxicillin in red because the patient has a penicillin allergy; the doctor knows it was a childhood rash and prescribes anyway. The entry carries the drug and nothing else. Six months later, after an anaphylaxis, the coroner asks whether the warning was shown and why it was overridden. The record cannot say; `instructions_text` is the only place, and nobody puts it there. The same for a duplicate CBC and a 10x dose. This is where "nothing clinical is refused" is incomplete: refusing is wrong, not recording the override is also wrong.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 04 rule 4: "**Nothing clinical is refused for safety reasons.** An allergy match, a duplicate request, a dose out of range: the screen warns inline; the function writes." and prescription: "Never refuses an allergy match or an interaction: the screen underlines in red." `write_prescription(…)` and `write_request(…)` have no parameter for a warning or an override reason.
gaps.fix: Additive parameter `warnings[] {kind (allergy | duplicate | dose | interaction), text, override_text}` on `write_prescription` and `write_request` (signatures only grow), copied into `data.warnings[]`; the medication row in `read_record` shows ⚠ when its latest entry carries an overridden allergy warning. Also tidy rule 4's wording: the spec already has clinical refusals (`none_known` with active rows, `prn` without reason, `patient_died` on `write_request`) — say "the only refusals are the ones each type lists" and add `patient_died` to `write_prescription`, which today accepts a prescription for a dead patient while a request is refused.
gaps.skeptic: The specialist is right that a structured override needs a new parameter: `write_prescription` and `write_request` shape `data` from fixed parameters and rule 1 gives the client no way to add a key. But the convention already exists: a `note` (`kind = other`) in the same `write_set`, tied by `written_with_id`, is how "penicillin: childhood rash, prescribing anyway" is recorded now, and a coroner reads it in the same timeline card. No clinic fails without `warnings[]`; the warning itself is computed by the client (04: "the screen underlines in red"), so the server can only ever record what the client reports. The parameter is additive under B17 "signatures only grow" and belongs with 04's later "interaction data (a pack)", when there are warnings worth recording. Severity and belongs stand. The `patient_died` inconsistency is real and one word: `write_request` and `open_visit` refuse it, `write_prescription` does not; add it when the function is written, since a dead patient is structural, not a safety refusal.

gaps.title: Orphaned drafts: a consultation can be silently undocumented
gaps.scenario: A doctor sees a patient, types the note and two prescriptions, clicks Back to queue for a phone call, and never returns. The visit is swept to `pending` at 12 h; the drafts sit in `drafts`, visible to nobody but her, forever. The next day another doctor opens the chart: no note, no prescriptions, no sign anything was typed. There is no list of unsent work anywhere. This is the unsigned-notes hazard in openCare's terms and it is the most likely daily failure.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05 rule 3: "**Today is a draft until Done.** Everything typed in a consult is a `drafts` row (autosaved, survives a reload) and reaches the record as one `write_set`." Known limits: "drafts are per user (two users editing one visit each see their own Today)". Spec 01 `drafts entry_id · author_id · patient_id · visit_id · type · service_id · reply_to_id · data` has no read function.
gaps.fix: `read_drafts(organization_id, department_id null = mine)` under `read:queue` (a new function); the queue footer gains "unsent" beside "away"; `read_visit_queue` rows carry `has_drafts` (return shapes may grow). The sweep is untouched: a visit with drafts still goes pending, but it is now visible as unfinished work.
gaps.skeptic: Genuine and uncovered. `drafts` is "outside the record" (01) with no function over it in 01's list at all, although 05 needs one for the author ("autosaved, survives a reload") and "the app never touches tables"; no pack can supply it (no privilege on core tables, no public draft read to wrap); 03's known limits already admit "a forgotten consult with nothing out stays open, invisible, for 14 days". Nobody but the author can see unsent work. The fix is additive as the specialist says: `has_drafts` on `read_visit_queue` rows (return shapes may grow) and an "unsent" count in the queue footer. Two corrections: keep draft content private to its author (a draft is not in the record), so any department-level read returns counts per visit, not text; and add the author's own `save_draft`/`read_drafts` to 01's function list, because 05 cannot work without them. No table or locked rule changes; the sweep is untouched.

gaps.title: Erasure has no gate, no retention guard, no legal hold, and a restore resurrects the erased
gaps.scenario: A patient asks for erasure under GDPR Art. 17 two years after treatment; the statute requires ten years' retention and the hospital is mid-litigation. `erase_patient` is "private", so nobody knows who may call it or under what MFA; nothing refuses an erasure inside the retention period; nothing marks a record as held; and a point-in-time restore after the erase brings the patient back with the `erasures` row gone.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 01 upkeep: "erase_patient (the only delete path: drafts and the record tables, then `patient_changes`, `visit_steps`, `visits`, `patient_identifiers`, `patients` … then the `erasures` row — spec 03)"; spec 01 appendix: "The private `erase_patient(patient_id, reason)` is the only delete path." and "After a point-in-time restore, the client and middleware outboxes refill the record." — but not the erasure.
gaps.fix: Write the rule now, build with merge: public `erase_patient(patient_id, reason_text)` under `manage:patients` + MFA (the action spec 03 already plans); refuses `retention_not_met` while any entry is younger than `organizations.retention_years` (additive column) unless `reason_text` names a listed override (`wrong_person`, `test_data`); refuses `legal_hold` while `patients.held_reason_text` (additive, set by `manage:patients`) is set; `erasures` gains `record_number` and `reason_text` (copied before the patient row goes); the `erasures` table is in every off-site backup copy and a documented post-restore step re-runs `erase_patient` for every row newer than the restore point. Residency itself needs nothing: it is the project's region.
gaps.skeptic: `erase_patient` is explicitly "written as rules now, built later" in 01 and 03, and 02 adds "`erase_patient` telling packs". Its only Phase 0 dependency, the insert-only trigger's transaction-local exception, is already in the 01 appendix (invariant 1). Every guard the specialist wants is an additive column (`organizations.retention_years`, `patients.held_reason_text`) or a refusal on a function that does not exist yet; the gate can be `manage:patients` + MFA exactly as 03 already uses for merge; the `erasures` columns are unlocked. Retention periods and Art. 17(3) exemptions are the organization's policy, not a core constant to fix now. The point-in-time restore resurrecting an erased patient is real but is a runbook line (keep `erasures` in the off-site copy; re-run `erase_patient` for every row newer than the restore point), operations, not schema. Nothing to write before Phase 0.

gaps.title: Controlled-drug e-prescribing: MFA at signing cannot be enforced by core or by a pack
gaps.scenario: A hospital e-prescribes oxycodone through a Pharmacy pack to an outside pharmacy. DEA EPCS (and equivalents) require the application to authenticate the prescriber with two factors at the moment of signing, and to record it. `write:prescription` passes at `aal1`; core does not know the drug is controlled (drug codes are "validated by form only"); a pack cannot refuse a core write; a client-side prompt is not enforcement.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 06 known limits: "a pack cannot refuse a core write (a controlled-drug rule is a warning in its screen, not a block)"; spec 02 Access: "`manage:` also needs MFA (`aal2`)" — the only MFA rule, keyed by verb; spec 04: "problem and drug codes are validated by form only and copied with their name".
gaps.fix: Additive parameter `is_controlled` on `write_prescription` (signatures only grow), declared by the client from the Pharmacy pack's catalogue; when true, `require_access` demands `aal2`, refuses `mfa_required` otherwise (a structural refusal, consistent with rule 4), and the function copies `data.signed_aal = 2`. The signed payload stays a file (01 appendix Y5). On paper scripts, where the wet signature is the legal instrument, nothing is needed for the first target.
gaps.skeptic: The spec already places the legal instrument outside the `prescription` entry: 01 appendix Y5 "Signed bytes are a file". Under EPCS the application that signs and transmits must authenticate with two factors; that application is the e-prescribing pack's sign-and-send flow (its own function plus an Edge Function for transmission, the pattern `invite` already uses), not `write_prescription`, which records clinical intent. A pack function may require step-up itself by reading the JWT's `aal` from `current_setting('request.jwt.claims')`, which names no core table, needs no `auth` USAGE and trips nothing in test 5's static scan, and refuse in its own function; 06 forbids refusing a core write, not the pack's own. The first target writes paper scripts (04: "Without one it is a paper script"), an in-house Pharmacy pack dispenses without DEA transmission, and US EPCS is speculative for two years. If core enforcement is ever wanted, the clean additive path is `actions.is_mfa` on the registry table so `require_access` keys MFA on the action rather than the verb, core-later; `is_controlled` on `write_prescription` is not needed.

gaps.title: Downtime recovery: one refused item blocks every other patient's writes
gaps.scenario: The connection drops for two hours; a doctor sees eight patients and Dones each (outbox). On reconnect the third set is refused (`request_not_open`: the consult was cancelled meanwhile). The outbox "stops at the first refusal": five other patients' notes and prescriptions are not in the record until she resolves item three, and she has gone home. gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 05 known limits: "the outbox replays in order and stops at the first refusal, which the user must resolve"; spec 05 Cross-cutting: "This is the whole offline story in v1"; spec 03: `record_number` "Mints … on insert only"; spec 05 Print: "nothing is stored" (no downtime viewer for a ward).
gaps.fix: Amend 05's outbox rule before the client is built: order is per patient (every `write_set` is one patient and all-or-nothing, so sets of different patients are independent); a refused set parks with its reason and the rest replay. Add one paragraph of downtime procedure: registration and arrivals go on a paper form and are entered afterwards with `occurred_at` backdated ("the client sends the age of an act" already allows it); a ward downtime viewer (a periodic printed or cached summary per inpatient) is the Admissions pack's job.
gaps.skeptic: 05's known limit "the outbox replays in order and stops at the first refusal, which the user must resolve" is wrong as a rule, not merely limited: every `write_set` is one patient and all-or-nothing, `mark_visit` is per visit, so sets of different patients have no ordering dependency; a refused set should park with its reason while the rest replay, and the only order that matters is within a patient (`replaces_id`, a `change` after its `start`). Together with gap 6 this is how five consultations vanish onto one laptop. Amend 05 to "in order per patient" before `src/core`'s outbox is written; no schema, no signature, nothing in Phase 0. The rest of the specialist's fix is not spec content: the paper procedure is a runbook (backdating already works through "the client sends the age of an act"; `arrived_at` cannot be backdated because "the click is the act", a cosmetic known limit), and a ward downtime viewer is the Admissions pack's.

gaps.title: `read_patient` reveals every department the patient ever visited, unaudited
gaps.scenario: A receptionist searches an ex-partner's name (allowed, `read:patient`), clicks the hit, and `read_patient` returns every visit with its department: Psychiatry 2024, GUM 2025. No `record_reads` row is written because "search is not a record read". The snooper never opens the chart and never appears in the audit.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 03 rule 6: "**Search is not a record read.** It returns the row, identifiers, open visits and open consults." and the reads paragraph: "**read_patient** adds every visit and the changes. Neither writes a `record_reads` row." The search-hit `open_visits[]` is already limited to "departments the caller may `read:queue`"; the full visit list in `read_patient` is not.
gaps.fix: Amend 03: `read_patient` returns visits only for departments the caller may `read:queue` (the same rule search hits already use), or writes a `record_reads` row when it returns them all. `read_patients` stays unaudited: a list of names is the desk's job. No signature change.

The spec's own defence, "A visit holds no clinical fact", does not survive a department name beside a date. Fix as the specialist says: `read_patient` returns visits for departments the caller may `read:queue`, the same rule as the hit, no signature change. At the first target there is one department and no exposure, so it does not gate Phase 0; but `read_patient` is written in Phase 0, so decide it while writing the function rather than narrowing a shipped read later.

gaps.title: Duplicates and look-alikes warn only at registration; at every later arrival the desk sees nothing
gaps.scenario: A patient was registered twice in March (the desk clicked New instead of Use this). In June an allergy is recorded on record B. In September he arrives, the desk searches, picks record A, the doctor prescribes the allergen: the banner shows no allergy and no hint that a second record exists. Meanwhile two present patients named Mohammed Ali sit in the same waiting band with nothing but a record number to tell them apart. `merge_patients` is built later, so the duplicate cannot be fixed before go-live.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 03 rule 5: "**Registration never blocks.** Duplicates warn; identifiers are not unique; the desk decides." Spec 05 Reception: "shows possible duplicates beneath the form as a warning with a **Use this** button, never a block" — the warning exists only in the New-patient form. Spec 03 built-later: "`merge_patients` … `manage:patients`, MFA".
gaps.fix: `read_patients` hits and `read_record.patient` carry `possible_duplicates[] {patient_id, record_number, reason (identifier | name_year | phone)}` (return shapes may grow) so the warning appears at every Here and in the visit banner; a client rule in 05 marks queue rows whose `plain_name` matches another present row. Ship `merge_patients` before the first go-live, not later: at 50 patients a day the first duplicate arrives within weeks.
gaps.skeptic: The duplicate is visible at every later arrival already: `read_patients` returns both records as two exact hits ("Exact hits first, 20 rows"), and 03's appendix defines the registration warning as nothing more than "this function called from the form with the typed family name, birth year and phone", so the client may make the same call from a hit and from the visit banner today with no spec change; `possible_duplicates[]` is a convenience, not a gap. Same-name marking in a queue is a client rule. `merge_patients` is a stated later rule with its refusals already written (`visit_open`, `manage:patients`, MFA, `patient_id = ANY(ids)`); shipping it before go-live rather than after is a schedule decision the owner should probably take, but it is not a spec gap and touches nothing in Phase 0.

gaps.title: A wrong merge that lived for a month cannot be fully undone, and the spec does not say what the residue is
gaps.scenario: Two patients are merged in error; for five weeks results, notes and prescriptions land on the survivor. `unmerge_patient` clears the pointer. Every entry written in those weeks stays on the survivor (`patient_id` is never rewritten) and the other patient's record is missing them; nobody is told which entries are in doubt.
gaps.where_it_breaks: Spec 03 appendix: "`unmerge_patient` undoes nothing else because nothing moved." Spec 01 appendix: `patient_id` "exactly one patient; never rewritten, even on merge"; spec 01 known limits: "a strike cannot be undone".
gaps.fix: Write the rule now: `unmerge_patient` returns the entries written for the survivor between the merge and the unmerge `patient_changes` rows; `read_record.patient` carries `unmerged_on` and that count until a clinician has struck and re-entered (as `source = import`, with the original `occurred_at`) whatever belongs to the other patient. No table change; the pre-merge history is already clean thanks to literal `patient_id`.
gaps.skeptic: `unmerge_patient` is built later, and the residue is the price of the locked rule that `patient_id` is "never rewritten, even on merge", which is what keeps the pre-merge history clean. The correction path is already the record's own: strike with `entered_in_error` (04's display line is literally "Struck: wrong patient") and re-enter for the right patient. The list of entries in doubt is derivable now with existing calls: `patient_changes` carries the merge and unmerge rows with their times, and `read_entries(patient_id, before_at, …)` pages that window. A banner count is cosmetic. Add one sentence to 03's merge paragraph when `unmerge_patient` is written; no table, no signature.

gaps.title: The read audit is written by prefetch and cannot be read
gaps.scenario: A ward nurse opens the ward queue; spec 05 prefetches read_record for the 40 present patients and each call inserts a record_reads row. A machine vitals write every 15 minutes signals record:<patient>, every open client refetches, and each refetch is another row. Across 20 wards and 1,500 users the audit grows by roughly a million rows a day, every one saying a person opened a chart they never looked at. When the privacy officer asks who looked at a minister's chart the answer is 'everyone who had a queue open', and there is no function to ask it anyway; no pack can add one because packs hold nothing on core tables.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 05 Cross-cutting: 'Opening a queue calls `read_record` for everyone present'; spec 02 Access: '`read_record` inserts a `record_reads` row; the other record reads raise `record_not_open` without one in the last 12 hours'; spec 02 Functions lists `read_settings_changes (manage:organization)` but no reader for `record_reads`; spec 06 rule 4: 'no privilege on any core table'.
gaps.fix: `read_record(patient_id, is_prefetch boolean default false)`: with true it writes no `record_reads` row and opens nothing; the click on a prefetched chart calls `read_record` again (served from cache, the call in the background) and that call writes the row and opens the 12-hour window. Add `read_record_reads(patient_id, since_at)` and `read_record_reads_by(user_id, since_at)` under `manage:organization`. All additive; no table changes.
gaps.skeptic: The pollution is real as written: spec 05 Cross-cutting 'Opening a queue calls `read_record` for everyone present' meets spec 02 Access '`read_record` inserts a `record_reads` row', so a ward queue writes 40 audit rows per open and one more per `record:<patient>` refetch, and no reader exists (spec 02 lists `read_settings_changes` only). But nothing structural is missing: `record_reads` gains no column. The fix is (a) one sentence in spec 05 scoping prefetch to screens that open charts; the sentence already says 'the 30 open charts of a clinic', and spec 03's appendix (line 291) had already rejected 'prefetching every present record' once, so spec 05 reinstating it is the thing to correct in words; (b) a defaulted `is_prefetch` parameter on `read_record` and a `read_record_reads` under `manage:organization`, both permitted later by 'public signatures only grow' (spec 02 CI list, spec 06 test 10). Severity is overstated for the first target: a clinic's 30 rows per queue open are bounded, and the 15-minute machine vitals feed the scenario assumes cannot exist, because a machine 'writes only replies to open requests sent there' (02 appendix line 49) and spec 01 known limits say 'no machine streams in the record'. Nothing in Phase 0 changes.

gaps.title: One serial runner for every pack and every organization, and no lag signal
gaps.scenario: Billing, Pharmacy and Imaging are on; 20,000 entries a day become 60,000 pack_calls rows, 3 a second at peak. Healthy packs at 20 ms a row are fine. Then Imaging's after_write loses an index at 20M rows and takes 3 s: the single runner connection does one or two rows per 5-second tick for every pack and every organization in the database; Billing's holds land minutes after the send, so every request started meanwhile is 'charged unpaid' for the whole backlog; nobody notices, because the only health signal is a parked count on a settings page and lag is measured nowhere.

By the tick interval plus queue depth'; 'Pack health is visible: parked rows per pack on the Organization page' is the whole monitoring story.
gaps.fix: One `cron.job` per row of `packs WHERE is_called_after_write` (`CALL core.run_pack_calls('<pack>')`, `next_pack_call(pack)`), so a slow pack starves only itself; B11 lists the jobs by rule instead of by count. Add `read_health(organization_id)` → {pending, oldest_pending_age, parked_by_pack, runner_last_tick_at, sweep_last_run_at} under `manage:organization` so ops can scrape and alert. The per-pack job is the Phase-0 part (the procedure, `next_pack_call` and B11 are Phase-0 objects); `read_health` is additive.
gaps.skeptic: Specialist's 'core-before-phase-0' is wrong. The head-of-line effect exists only in a narrow band: a pack that is slow under the 5 s `statement_timeout` at sustained volume. Over 5 s, 02 appendix line 128 already handles it ('A `query_canceled` … ends the procedure; the cancelled row's try is already committed, so it sinks behind fresh rows'), so rule 7's 'fails, sleeps or lies' is kept; 'slow' is simply not among them and belongs in spec 02 known limits as one sentence. Cross-organization starvation is moot by a stated rule: spec 01 decide-now 'no partitioning (scale out = database per organization)'. Nothing here is a Phase-0 rewrite: `core.run_pack_calls`, `core.next_pack_call` and `core.finish_pack_call` are private ('`pack_runner` only', not in the golden public-signatures file), `pack_calls` already carries `pack` in its primary key so per-pack or round-robin selection needs no column, and B11 hashes `cron.job` by content, so adding jobs later is a test edit. `read_health` is additive: `read_organization` already returns 'the parked `pack_calls` count per pack' (02 appendix line 110); pending count and oldest age are two more fields. At the clinic's ~500 entries a day with two packs, a serial runner at 20 ms a row has 100x headroom. Build it serial, write the limit down, split when a pack measurably needs it.

gaps.title: A go-live import queues ten years of history for every pack
gaps.scenario: 500k patients and 20M entries are loaded through the write functions as an `importer` user with Billing and Pharmacy switched on. `write_entry` inserts one pack_calls row per pack per entry: 40M rows. The serial runner clears them in weeks; Billing's after_write charges 2019's CBCs; Pharmacy's stock moves for dispenses that happened in another system. The appendix says imports send no signal, but nothing says they send no pack call, and the import unit (per patient, parallel) is a table-row remark, not a contract.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 01 `write_entry`: 'insert one `pack_calls` row per pack that is on for the organization, is called after write, and did not itself write the entry'; spec 02 appendix invariant 13 lists the exceptions 'never on retry, rebuild or step' — import is not among them; spec 01 appendix T12: 'system users, one transaction per patient, derived ids, no signal, no requests, flags as given'.
gaps.fix: One clause in `write_entry` and in invariant 13: no `pack_calls` row and no signal when `source = 'import'`. State in spec 06 that a pack wanting history backfills through public reads on its own. Write the import contract into spec 01: one transaction per patient, parallel across patients (the patient lock permits it), `recorded_at` stamped, original time in `data` — so 20M entries is a weekend, not a week. A rule change in a Phase-0 function that Billing (specced next) is designed against.
gaps.skeptic: Specialist's 'core-before-phase-0' is wrong; the specs already give the go-live path. `write_entry` inserts a `pack_calls` row only 'per pack that is on for the organization' (spec 01), so an import run before packs are enabled queues nothing; spec 06 Enable then runs `rebuild_record`, whose updaters replay lists while `after_write` is 'never on rebuild', so no charges for 2019's CBCs and no stock moves. That is the natural order of any go-live (load, enable, open the doors), and packs must be off during import anyway: the importer holds only `write:` actions and a pack-typed write with the pack off raises `pack_off` through `require_pack`; pack-typed history (charges, stock, dispenses) is the pack's own data under spec 06 rule 5 and is the pack's own import. The residual, a re-import after go-live with packs on, is one predicate (`AND source <> 'import'`) in the private `write_entry` insert plus one clause in 02 appendix invariant 13, neither a table nor a public-signature change, and can land the week a second import is scheduled. The import contract the specialist wants 'written into spec 01' is already in its appendix: T12 'system users, one transaction per patient, derived ids, no signal, no requests, flags as given', line 496 'Importers derive ids from legacy keys', line 616 'An import stamps a new `recorded_at` and keeps the original in `data`'. Billing's `after_write` is idempotent on `entry_id` either way, so nothing in Billing's spec depends on this.

gaps.title: Machines cannot read and nothing can leave the database
gaps.scenario: 30 analysers, a PACS, an ADT feed, patient SMS and the on-call pager. An interface engine needs to pull the lab's open orders with a machine login, but a machine may hold only `write:` in one department; `service_role` has no table privilege and exactly two functions; pack roles have no USAGE on `net`. So a notifications row a pack writes can be delivered by nobody, an LIS can only push results for orders it never learned about, and machine logins themselves are 'built later' — the day-one need of any hospital lab.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 02 appendix S13: 'a machine user writes only replies to open requests sent to its one department, or drafts; no `read:`, `mark:`, `manage:`, no everywhere'; B9: '`service_role` exactly on `create_organization` and `link_login` and no table privilege anywhere'; pack roles: 'no USAGE on `net`'; spec 02 Written as rules now, built later: 'machine logins with the first analyser'.
gaps.fix: Widen the machine rule the way the reception machine already is: a machine may hold `read:queue`, and a pack's own `read:` actions, in its one department. State in spec 06 the outbound pattern: a pack exposes `<key>_read_pending()` and a machine user of that pack's department drains it, so no pack ever needs `net`. Ship `link_machine_login` (service_role, called by an MFA'd `manage:users` holder) in the Phase-0 Edge Function set instead of 'with the first analyser'. All additive.
gaps.skeptic: Machine logins are a stated later rule, spec 02 built-later 'machine logins with the first analyser', and the clinic's first analyser is a Phase-1-or-later event, not Phase 0; shipping `link_machine_login` in the Phase-0 Edge Function set is speculative structure. The widening the specialist wants already has its shape in the spec: spec 02 Core roles, 'or, in a `reception` department, holds `read:patient`, `read:queue` and `write:visit` there and on the departments it serves'. So 'a machine in a `laboratory` department may hold `read:queue` and its pack's own `read:` there' is one more clause in `save_user`'s machine rule and 02 appendix invariant 5, not a table change and not a rewrite; S13's confinement (one department, no `mark:`, no `manage:`, no everywhere) stays true. Outbound is by design, not omission: B9 pins `service_role` to two functions and pack roles have 'no USAGE on `net`'; the pattern is one sentence in spec 06 ('a pack that needs something delivered exposes `<key>_read_pending()`; a machine user of its department drains it') or the existing Edge Function set. Unidirectional analysers (tech keys the specimen number on the instrument, results pushed as replies to open requests) run under today's rule; host-query is the case the widening serves, and it can wait for the analyser that needs it.

gaps.title: A request sent outside can never be answered
gaps.scenario: A clinic sends 40 samples a week to a reference laboratory; a hospital group's central lab serves three organizations. The send-out is a request to an `is_outside` department; `write_result` needs `write:result` in that department; nobody may hold a role there. The result comes back as an unsolicited `write_result(request_id NULL)` plus a `Review result` request, and the original request stays open in `read_sent_outside` until someone cancels it with a reason. The system runs, but every send-out in the history ends `cancelled`, and turnaround, holds and the one review loop never see the answer.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 04 result: 'Caller must hold `write:result` in the request's `to_department_id`'; spec 02: '`outside` (created on first use; nobody holds a role there)' and '`user_roles` ... never on an outside department'; spec 02 Access widens only `read:queue` 'on an outside department for anyone holding it in the organization'.
gaps.fix: Give `write:result` (and `mark:cancelled`) the widening `read:queue` already has: when the request's destination `is_outside`, the gate passes for anyone holding the action anywhere in the organization; the reply's `department_id` is the filer's own, `source = outside`, `data.source_name` the provider. One clause in `require_access`; no table change. Spec 04's outside-result paragraph then covers solicited results too.
gaps.skeptic: Downgraded because the workflow is expressible under the gate as written; 'nobody may hold a role there' reads too much into the trigger. 02 appendix line 114: the caller passes when holding the action 'in `department_id` or everywhere'; invariant 5 refuses a `user_roles` row that names an `is_outside` department, and an everywhere row (`department_id NULL`) names none. So an everywhere holder of `write:result` (the owner, or the nurse or technician who files paper results in a five-department clinic) answers a send-out today, and spec 04's 'Caller must hold `write:result` in the request's `to_department_id`' is satisfied; that is exactly why O14 needed the `read:queue` widening only for department-scoped holders. The residual is real but small: the spec never says this in words, so an implementer who adds an 'outside means refuse' check breaks it, and a hospital will not want its send-out clerk holding `write:result` in every internal lab. Both are one clause in `require_access`: `write:result` (and `mark:cancelled`) pass on an `is_outside` destination for anyone holding them anywhere in the organization, the same widening `read:queue` has; the reply's `department_id` is the filer's own, `source = outside`, `data.source_name` the provider. This is the one item in the list an IM clinic meets in month one, so write the sentence into spec 04's result paragraph now and code it whenever `require_access` is built. Not a Phase-0 dependency and no table changes.

gaps.title: An organization-wide rebuild has no job
gaps.scenario: A release fixes `update_patient_medications`, or Pharmacy is switched on for a hospital with 500k patients and spec 06 says enable replays existing entries. `rebuild_record(patient_id)` is per patient under the patient lock; there is no batch, no progress, no resumability, and `save_organization_pack` is one MFA'd call under the API's 8-second limit. At 50 ms a patient that is seven hours of work nobody designed, and a crash at patient 300k starts from zero.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 06 Lifecycle, Enable: '`save_organization_pack` → one `organization_packs` row; ...; `rebuild_record` replays existing entries through its updater'; spec 01 appendix: 'The rebuild loop logs patients with a non-zero count, for clinical review' — the loop is named, not designed.

Add `core.rebuilds (organization_id, patient_id, list null, requested_at, done_at, changed_rows)` filled by `request_rebuild(organization_id, list)` under `manage:organization` and drained by a cron job in the runner's shape (SKIP LOCKED, 5 s timeout, per-patient commit), with progress in `read_health`. Additive table and job.
gaps.skeptic: Half of this is a wording fix the specialist gets right, and it costs nothing: spec 06 Enable's '`rebuild_record` replays existing entries through its updater' is a no-op by the specs' own rules, because the updater runs on corrections while a pack is off (spec 01 'With a pack off, its entries still render, trend and accept corrections'; spec 06 test 7) and a pack's list comes only from its own types (spec 06 rule 2, no reuse of a type key; the dispatch is `coalesce(entry_types.pack, 'core')`), so a list never rots between off and on. Strike the clause; `save_organization_pack` stays a plain `save_…` under the 8 s limit. The other half, a release that fixes an updater over 500k patients, is an ops script over an idempotent, per-patient, per-list-isolated function (02 appendix invariant 20; 01 appendix line 300 'returns the rows changed per table') whose resumability is `WHERE id > last` on `patients`; 01 appendix line 301 'The rebuild loop logs patients with a non-zero count' is that script. A `core.rebuilds` table and a cron job in the runner's shape is speculative structure until a rebuild takes longer than a night; at the clinic's scale it is minutes.

gaps.title: Support without impersonation has no dry-run gate
gaps.scenario: 1,500 users and 40 departments produce 'I can't see the ER queue' and 'my Done was refused' ten times a day. Support may not act as the person (rightly), `require_access` raises, but the ordinary role refusal has no name and no detail, and there is no way to ask 'would user X pass action Y on department Z, and through which role?' without being X. The helpdesk reads `settings_changes` and guesses.
gaps.where_it_breaks: spec 02 Access: 'no client and no pack can act as a person'; the named refusals across the specs are `unknown_action`, `pack_off`, `record_not_open`, `changed_since_read`, `last_administrator`, `visit_moved` — the plain 'no role in that department' refusal is unnamed; `read_settings_changes (manage:organization)` is the only support read.
gaps.fix: Name the refusal (`not_allowed`, detail `{action, department_id}`) and add `read_access(user_id, action, patient_id, department_id)` → `{passes, role_id, department_id, reason}` under `manage:users`: STABLE, writes nothing, evaluates the same predicate as the gate. Additive.
gaps.skeptic: Two things, neither structural. The unnamed refusal is a word the implementer must pick when `require_access` is written: 02 appendix line 114 names `unknown_action` for the first check and nothing for the last, and spec 05 matches on server reasons ('`already_replaced`, `request_not_open`…'), so the name and its detail `{action, department_id}` should be written into spec 02's gate paragraph now as a one-line amendment; that is naming, not a Phase-0 object or table. The dry-run is already expressible: `read_organization` returns 'users with roles, roles with actions' plus departments with served rows (02 appendix line 110), and the appendix says so at line 277, 'Rights are auditable in SQL: who holds what where is three joins', so a helpdesk with `read:organization` evaluates 'does X hold Y in Z or everywhere, or through `served_departments`' on the client without being X and without a new function. `read_access(…)` as a STABLE convenience that runs the gate's own predicate is additive if 1,500 users ever make the client-side check tedious; that scale is year 2+.

gaps.title: No write function carries `department_id`, and the only mechanism to supply it is on the rejected list
gaps.scenario: A doctor holding `doctor` in Internal Medicine and in the Diabetes clinic opens a visit and writes a note. `entries.department_id` must be set (CHECK `department_id IS NOT NULL OR source IN ('patient','import')`), the gate must be run for a department, `write_request` must check the service is 'offered to the caller's department', and `read_record.visit` is 'the caller's department's open visit' — but nothing in the call says which department.

Doing it now avoids a B17 arity change on nine functions later.
gaps.skeptic: Confirmed in the text. Every spec 04 signature (`write_note(id, patient_id, visit_id, kind, …)` and the other eight) lacks `department_id`; the 01 appendix CHECK `department_id IS NOT NULL OR source IN ('patient','import')` makes it mandatory on every staff entry; spec 04 needs 'the caller's department' in `write_request` (the served check), `write_note` ('an open consult request addressed to the caller's department') and `read_record.visit`; and 02 appendix O4 says a covering technician's reply carries the ER lab as its `department_id`, not the request's `to_department_id`, so even `write_result` cannot derive it. Spec 05 line 40 names `staff_active_department`, which 02 appendix section k rejects by name together with 'server-side "where am I"'; 03 boundary rule 1 forbids reading `visits`. Phase 0 cannot insert one staff fixture entry without this decision, and adding the parameter after B17's golden file exists costs a `removed` line per function plus an outbox shim. Fix as proposed: `department_id` on every `write_<type>`, on `write_set` (one for the set) and on `read_record`; a client-held choice, no server state; `drafts` gains the same column because 'committing a draft is a column-for-column copy'.

gaps.title: A pack migration under `SET ROLE pack_<key>` cannot insert registry rows or `ALTER TYPE request_step`, and core cannot pre-create a role for a pack it must not know
gaps.scenario: The Laboratory pack's first migration runs `SET ROLE pack_laboratory; insert into entry_types …; ALTER TYPE request_step ADD VALUE 'collected'`.
